### 14. user (2026-07-06T05:55:34.616Z)

===README===
# telegram-video-filter

A Telethon-based **userbot** that logs in as your own Telegram account, watches
new video messages across all the channels/groups you subscribe to, applies
configurable filters (duration, resolution, file size), and **forwards matching
videos to your Saved Messages** in real time.

> ⚠️ This project automates a **user** account (a "userbot") via MTProto. Keep
> volumes reasonable and respect Telegram's Terms of Service. You are
> responsible for your own account. See [`docs/adr/0001-userbot-over-botapi.md`](docs/adr/0001-userbot-over-botapi.md).

## Status

✅ **v1 complete** — all 6 build phases merged via PR. The app runs end-to-end:
bootstrap a user account → manager watches their channels → filters videos →
forwards matches to Saved Messages. See [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md) for the
build history and [`docs/runbook.md`](docs/runbook.md) to deploy.
phased build plan and current status.

## What it does (v1)

- Watches every channel/group your account is a member of — no per-channel setup.
- Reads video metadata **without downloading** the file (duration, width/height,
  size, MIME).
- Applies an **AND** of your filters, e.g.:
  - duration between 5s and 2h,
  - height ≥ 1080 (1080p or better),
  - size ≤ 2 GiB.
- Forwards each match to your **Saved Messages** in real time, or to a
  **channel you own** if you set `delivery_target` (per-user).
- **Never forwards the same video twice** — three-tier content dedup
  (message instance → Telegram `document.id` → metadata fingerprint) means
  a video cross-posted to 5 channels is delivered once. See
  [`docs/adr/0006-content-dedup.md`](docs/adr/0006-content-dedup.md).
- Supports multiple users (<100) on a single host, each with its own session,
  filters, delivery mode/target, and dedup state.

## What it does NOT do yet (v2+)

- Public-channel `/add @channel` join, manual-add ingestion.
- Scheduled digest delivery and on-demand `/list` / `/search`.
- ffprobe-based deep inspection (`/inspect`).
- Codec / keyword / MIME filters.

## Documentation

- [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md) — phased build plan, scope, verification.
- [`docs/design.md`](docs/design.md) — architecture, data model, control flow.
- [`docs/runbook.md`](docs/runbook.md) — deploy, onboard users, rotate
  sessions, handle flood waits.
- [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/) — Architecture Decision Records:
  - [0001 – Userbot over Bot API](docs/adr/0001-userbot-over-botapi.md)
  - [0002 – SQLite over PostgreSQL](docs/adr/0002-sqlite-over-postgres.md)
  - [0003 – Metadata-first probing](docs/adr/0003-metadata-first-probing.md)
  - [0004 – Pluggable delivery modes](docs/adr/0004-pluggable-delivery-modes.md)
  - [0005 – Per-user delivery target](docs/adr/0005-per-user-delivery-target.md)

## Quick start

See the [runbook](docs/runbook.md) for the full guide. In short:

```bash
cp .env.example .env        # set TG_API_ID, TG_API_HASH from my.telegram.org
docker compose up -d --build
python -m tg_video_filter.bootstrap   # interactive one-time login per user
docker compose restart app
```

## Tech stack

Python 3.11+ · [Telethon](https://docs.telethon.dev/) · aiosqlite (SQLite) ·
pydantic / pydantic-settings · Docker · pytest · ruff.

===pyproject===
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "tg-video-filter"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Telethon userbot that filters Telegram channel videos by duration, resolution, and size, and forwards matches to Saved Messages."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = { text = "TBD" }
authors = [{ name = "avidullu" }]
keywords = ["telegram", "telethon", "userbot", "video", "filter"]
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Private :: Do Not Upload",
]

# Runtime dependencies. Pinned to compatible ranges; bump deliberately.
dependencies = [
    "telethon>=1.36,<2.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.20,<1.0",
    "pydantic>=2.7,<3.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.3,<3.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0,<2.0",
    # Native crypto acceleration for Telethon (optional but strongly recommended;
    # without it Telethon falls back to slower pure-Python encryption).
    "cryptg>=0.4,<1.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.2,<9.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23,<1.0",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0,<7.0",
    "ruff>=0.5,<0.7",
    "pre-commit>=3.7,<5.0",
]

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/avidullu/telegram-video-filter"
Documentation = "https://github.com/avidullu/telegram-video-filter/blob/main/docs/design.md"

# Tell hatchling where the package lives (src layout).
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/tg_video_filter"]

# --- pytest -----------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--cov=tg_video_filter",
    "--cov-report=term-missing",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    # Telethon/aiosqlite may emit benign DeprecationWarnings; surface but don't fail.
    "default::DeprecationWarning:telethon.*",
]

# --- ruff (lint + format) ---------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]
extend-exclude = ["data"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # isort
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
    "RUF",  # ruff-specific
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line length handled by formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["B017"]  # allow pytest.raises(Exception) patterns in tests
"src/tg_video_filter/backfill.py" = ["RUF006"]  # asyncio.create_task stored in named var; GC keeps ref

[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true

# --- coverage floor ---------------------------------------------------------
[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["src/tg_video_filter"]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",

1	# ADR 0011: Provider-neutral domain schema (Track B)
2	
3	- **Status**: Accepted (Question 1 → Option 1A; Question 2 → Option 2A; PR #34)
4	- **Date**: 2026-07-06
5	- **Decision owner**: project owner
6	- **Tracking issue**: #27 (Track B of the provider-neutral umbrella, #25)
7	- **Depends on**: ADR 0010 (Track A — `accounts` + `telegram_sessions`, merged in #33)
8	- **Blocks**: #28 (Track C — delivery/routing), #29 (Track D — commands), and indirectly #30 (Track E)
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	ADR 0010 split `users` into `accounts` (product identity) + `telegram_sessions`
13	(MTProto credential). That unblocked the *identity* dimension. This ADR
14	tackles the **content dimension**: how to represent sources, content items,
15	policies, destinations, routes, and delivery attempts in a provider-neutral
16	way, so that the system can ingest from Telegram today and from WhatsApp
17	(or any future provider) later without another schema rewrite.
18	
19	### What we have today (post-Track-A)
20	
21	| Table | Meaning | Provider-coupling |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `accounts` | Product identity (ADR 0010) | provider-neutral (`provider` column) |
24	| `telegram_sessions` | Optional MTProto session (ADR 0010) | Telegram-specific by design |
25	| `channels` | A Telegram channel/chat an account is a member of | **Telegram-specific** (`channel_id` is a Telegram id) |
26	| `videos` | A seen Telegram video message + metadata | **Telegram-specific** (`message_id`, `document_id` are Telegram ids) |
27	| `filter_config` | Per-account JSON blob of `FilterConfig` | provider-neutral in shape, but scoped per-account not per-source |
28	
29	The dedup logic (ADR 0006) is **3-tier and Telegram-specific**:
30	- Tier 0: `(user_id, channel_id, message_id)` — same Telegram message.
31	- Tier 1: `(user_id, document_id)` — same Telegram file forwarded across channels.
32	- Tier 2: `(user_id, size_bytes, duration_s, height, width)` — re-upload fingerprint.
33	
34	### What we need
35	
36	The umbrella (#25) introduces six concepts: `Source`, `ContentItem`, `Policy`,
37	`Destination`, `Route` (`routing_rules`), and `DeliveryAttempt`. This ADR
38	defines the schema for each, the **two open design questions** that gate the
39	schema, and the migration path from the current tables.
40	
41	## The two decisions I need from you
42	
43	### Question 1: `ContentItem.dedup_key` — how does provider-neutral dedup relate to ADR 0006?
44	
45	The current 3-tier dedup is Telegram-specific (`document_id` is a Telegram
46	concept). A provider-neutral `ContentItem` needs a dedup story that works
47	across providers. Three options:
48	
49	#### Option 1A (recommended): tiered lookup that wraps ADR 0006's tiers
50	
51	Keep ADR 0006's three tiers but generalize them behind a single
52	`dedup_key` column on `content_items`:
53	
54	```
55	content_items.dedup_key TEXT NOT NULL
56	```
57	
58	The *value* of `dedup_key` is computed by an explicit decision tree at
59	ingestion time, provider by provider. The tree is ordered strongest-key
60	first and each branch is **guarded so partial metadata can never collapse
61	to a degenerate key** (e.g. `tg:fp:0:0:0:0`):
62	
63	- **Telegram:**
64	  1. If `document_id` is present → `dedup_key = "tg:doc:{document_id}"`.
65	  2. Else if **all four** fingerprint fields (`size_bytes`, `duration_s`,
66	     `height`, `width`) are present → `dedup_key = "tg:fp:{size}:{dur}:{h}:{w}"`.
67	  3. Else → `dedup_key = "tg:msg:{source_id}:{provider_message_id}"`
68	     (Tier 0; the source/channel id is required because Telegram
69	     `message_id` is only unique within a channel, not across sources).
70	- **Future WhatsApp:** `dedup_key = "wa:msg:{message_id}"` (WhatsApp message
71	  ids are globally unique per account) or `"wa:sha256:{blob_hash}"` if WA
72	  exposes a content hash.
73	
74	The guard in step 2 (all four fields required) is what prevents the
75	partial-metadata collision the first draft of this ADR allowed. The pure
76	`compute_dedup_key(provider, *, document_id, source_id, provider_message_id,
77	size_bytes, duration_s, height, width)` function that implements this tree
78	gets its own unit tests in the implementation PR, including cases for
79	partial/null metadata.
80	
81	A **partial unique index** on `(account_id, dedup_key) WHERE dedup_key IS NOT NULL`
82	replaces the current Tier-1 index and enforces per-account dedup at the DB
83	level, regardless of provider.
84	
85	**Why recommended:**
86	- Zero new bandwidth — all keys are computed from metadata already extracted
87	  (honors ADR 0003's no-download principle).
88	- The provider prefix (`tg:` / `wa:`) makes cross-provider collisions
89	  structurally impossible.
90	- Existing `videos` rows migrate cleanly: `dedup_key` is computed from their
91	  existing `document_id` / metadata columns during the migration.
92	- Supersedes ADR 0006 cleanly: the three tiers become *one* column with
93	  provider-specific derivation rules, documented in the migration.
94	
95	**Costs:**
96	- The migration must compute `dedup_key` for every existing `videos` row
97	  (cheap — pure SQL string building, no I/O).
98	- The `dedup_key` derivation logic lives in code (a pure function per
99	  provider), not in the schema. This is a feature, but it means the
100	  derivation rules need their own unit tests.
101	
102	#### Option 1B: content hash (SHA-256 of downloaded bytes)
103	
104	`dedup_key = sha256(downloaded_content)`. Cryptographically strong,
105	provider-agnostic, catches re-encodes that 1A misses.
106	
107	**Rejected** — violates ADR 0003 (metadata-first, no download in the hot
108	path). Downloading every incoming video to hash it would multiply bandwidth
109	and latency by orders of magnitude. Could be added later as an optional
110	deep-inspect stage (deferred to Track F per #31).
111	
112	#### Option 1C: provider-assigned only (drop Tier 2)
113	
114	`dedup_key = "tg:doc:{document_id}"` always; no metadata fingerprint
115	fallback. Simpler, but loses Tier-2 dedup for re-uploads that get a new
116	`document.id` — a real and common case (someone re-encodes and re-uploads
117	the same video to a different channel).
118	
119	**Recommendation: 1A.** It preserves the dedup quality of ADR 0006, generalizes cleanly, and honors the no-download constraint.
120	
121	---
122	
123	### Question 2: `Policy` ↔ existing `filter_config` — rename, or wrap?
124	
125	The codebase already has `filter_config.config_json` (one row per account,
126	holding a `FilterConfig` JSON blob — see `models.py` and ADR 0005). The
127	umbrella introduces a `Policy` concept. They overlap. Two options:
128	
129	#### Option 2A (recommended): `Policy` *generalizes* `filter_config` (rename + extend)
130	
131	`policies` is a new table; `filter_config` is migrated into it. One account
132	can own multiple policies (enables per-route filter overrides from ADR
133	0009), with a `DEFAULT policy` per account for the no-rules-configured case.
134	
135	```
136	policies (
137	    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
138	    account_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
139	    name         TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- e.g. "default", "reggae-route"
140	    config_json  TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- the FilterConfig blob (Phase 1)
141	    is_default   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,        -- one per account (UNIQUE partial idx)
142	    created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
143	    updated_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
144	    UNIQUE (account_id, name)
145	);
146	```
147	
148	**Phase 1** (this track): `config_json` holds exactly today's `FilterConfig`
149	JSON — the rename is purely structural. **Phase 2** (Track F, deferred):
150	`config_json` grows to include topic preferences and security rules, but
151	that's behind the same column so no further migration.
152	
153	Migration: for each `filter_config` row, insert a `policies` row with
154	`name='default'`, `is_default=1`, `config_json=<the existing blob>`. Drop
155	`filter_config` after the migration (keep `filter_config_deprecated` for one
156	release, mirroring ADR 0010's safety-net pattern).
157	
158	**Why recommended:**
159	- `Policy` becomes the single home for "what to filter/enrich" — no second
160	  overlapping concept. Today's `FilterConfig` is just the Phase-1 shape.
161	- Enables ADR 0009's per-route filter overrides (`routing_rules.policy_id`)
162	  without a second migration later.
163	- The existing `db.load_filter_config(account_id)` / `save_filter_config`
164	  become thin shims over `policies WHERE account_id=? AND is_default=1`,
165	  mirroring the Track-A `User` shim pattern — backwards-compatible.
166	
167	**Costs:**
168	- One more table migration. `filter_config` → `policies` is a rename+extend.
169	- The `FilterConfig` Pydantic model stays (it's the Phase-1 config shape);
170	  `Policy` is the *container* (name, owner, default flag) around it. Two
171	  models, not one — but they compose cleanly.
172	
173	#### Option 2B: keep `filter_config` as-is; `Policy` is a wrapping layer
174	
175	Don't touch `filter_config`. `policies` references a `filter_config` row
176	plus adds enrichment/security stages as separate columns.
177	
178	**Rejected** — creates two overlapping concepts (`filter_config` for the
179	v1 rules, `policies` for "everything else"), which is exactly the
180	conflation the umbrella exists to dissolve. We'd be back here in a year
181	merging them.
182	
183	**Recommendation: 2A.** One concept, one table, phased growth via the same JSON column.
184	
185	---
186	
187	## Proposed schema (assuming 1A + 2A)
188	
189	### `sources` (generalizes `channels`)
190	
191	A configured place we ingest from. Maps 1:1 to today's per-account
192	`channels` rows for Telegram; future providers add their own source kinds.
193	
194	```
195	sources (
196	    id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
197	    account_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
198	    provider          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'telegram',
199	    provider_source_id TEXT NOT NULL,        -- Telegram channel_id; future: WA group id
200	    title             TEXT,
201	    kind              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'channel',  -- 'channel' | 'group' | 'feed'
202	    watched           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,       -- ADR 0009 selective scanning
203	    seen_first_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
204	    last_seen_at      TEXT,
205	    UNIQUE (account_id, provider, provider_source_id)
206	);
207	```
208	
209	`channels.user_id` (now → `accounts.id`) maps to `sources.account_id`;
210	`channels.channel_id` maps to `sources.provider_source_id`. The `watched`
211	flag (ADR 0009, deferred to Track E) is included here so Track E doesn't
212	need another migration.
213	
214	### `content_items` (generalizes `videos`)
215	
216	A normalized item discovered from any source. Phase 1 stores only videos
217	(matches today's `videos`); the columns are provider-neutral but the
218	Phase-1 migration only populates video fields.
219	
220	```
221	content_items (
222	    id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
223	    account_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
224	    source_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sources(id),
225	    provider          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'telegram',
226	    provider_message_id TEXT NOT NULL,       -- Telegram message_id; future: WA message id
227	    content_type      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'video',  -- 'video' | 'link' | 'article' | ...
228	    text              TEXT,                  -- caption / post text (nullable)
229	    link_url          TEXT,                  -- for link/article posts
230	    media_ref         TEXT,                  -- provider media reference (file path, blob id)
231	    document_id       TEXT,                  -- Telegram document.id (kept for TG-specific lookups)
232	    duration_s        INTEGER,
233	    width             INTEGER,
234	    height            INTEGER,
235	    size_bytes        INTEGER,
236	    mime_type         TEXT,
237	    dedup_key         TEXT NOT NULL,         -- ADR 0011 Question 1 (Option 1A)
238	    matched           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
239	    seen_at           TEXT NOT NULL,
240	    -- Tier-0 equivalent: provider_message_id is only unique within a source
241	    -- (a Telegram message_id is per-channel), so source_id is required to
242	    -- avoid false collisions across sources for the same account.
243	    UNIQUE (account_id, source_id, provider_message_id),
244	    UNIQUE (account_id, dedup_key)                        -- Tier-1/2 equivalent (Option 1A)
245	);
246	```
247	
248	**Note on `forwarded`:** dropped from `content_items`. Per-destination
249	delivery state moves to `delivery_attempts` (Track C, #28). For Phase 1
250	(before Track C lands), `content_items.matched` alone is sufficient —
251	delivery still goes to the single `delivery_target`, and the boolean
252	`forwarded` is retained temporarily on a *deprecated* `videos`-compat view
253	so the v1 delivery path keeps working. Track C removes it.
254	
255	### `policies` (generalizes `filter_config`) — Option 2A
256	
257	As specified in Question 2 above.
258	
259	### `destinations` (new — Track C will populate)
260	
261	Defined here so the schema is complete, but **Track C (#28) implements the
262	delivery layer**. Phase-1 presence is the table only (no delivery logic).
263	
264	```
265	destinations (
266	    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
267	    account_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
268	    provider    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'telegram',
269	    target      TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'me', '@username', chat id (ADR 0005)
270	    kind        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'saved',  -- 'saved' | 'channel' | 'chat'
271	    title       TEXT,
272	    is_output   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,      -- ADR 0009: distinguishes output channels
273	    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
274	    UNIQUE (account_id, provider, target)
275	);
276	```
277	
278	### `routing_rules` (new — Track C will populate)
279	
280	Per ADR 0009 (canonical name locked in issue #25).
281	
282	```
283	routing_rules (
284	    id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
285	    account_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
286	    source_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sources(id),
287	    policy_id      INTEGER,               -- nullable → use account's default policy
288	    destination_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES destinations(id),
289	    enabled        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
290	    priority       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
291	    created_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
292	    UNIQUE (account_id, source_id, destination_id)
293	);
294	```
295	
296	### `delivery_attempts` (new — Track C will populate)
297	
298	Per #28's idempotency requirement (unique index on
299	`(content_item_id, destination_id)`).
300	
301	```
302	delivery_attempts (
303	    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
304	    content_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES content_items(id),
305	    destination_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES destinations(id),
306	    route_id        INTEGER REFERENCES routing_rules(id),
307	    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- 'pending'|'delivered'|'failed'|'retrying'
308	    attempt_count   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
309	    last_error      TEXT,
310	    created_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
311	    delivered_at    TEXT,
312	    next_retry_at   TEXT,
313	    UNIQUE (content_item_id, destination_id)         -- ADR #28 idempotency
314	);
315	```
316	
317	## Migration strategy (integer-preserving, phased)
318	
319	This track lands **`sources`, `content_items`, and `policies`** only.
320	`destinations`, `routing_rules`, `delivery_attempts` are defined in the
321	schema (so the ADR is complete) but their tables are created empty and
322	populated by Track C. This keeps Track B focused and reviewable.
323	
324	### Migration `_migration_003_domain_schema` (idempotent)
325	
326	1. **Create** `sources`, `content_items`, `policies`, `destinations`,
327	   `routing_rules`, `delivery_attempts` (all `IF NOT EXISTS`).
328	2. **Backfill `sources`** from `channels`:
329	   `provider='telegram'`, `provider_source_id=channel_id`, `watched=1`
330	   (ADR 0009 backfill: already-seen channels stay watched).
331	3. **Backfill `content_items`** from `videos`, computing `dedup_key` via the
332	   explicit decision tree from Option 1A (every branch reachable, no
333	   `COALESCE(...,0)` collapsing partial metadata to a degenerate key):
334	   - If `document_id IS NOT NULL`:
335	     `dedup_key = 'tg:doc:' || document_id`.
336	   - Else if `size_bytes IS NOT NULL AND duration_s IS NOT NULL AND height IS NOT NULL AND width IS NOT NULL`:
337	     `dedup_key = 'tg:fp:' || size_bytes || ':' || duration_s || ':' || height || ':' || width`.
338	   - Else (Tier-0 fallback; partial or missing media metadata):
339	     `dedup_key = 'tg:msg:' || source_id || ':' || provider_message_id`,
340	     where `source_id` is the joined `sources.id` for the row's legacy
341	     `channel_id` and `provider_message_id` is the legacy `message_id`.
342	
343	   The implementation PR must include migration tests that seed rows hitting
344	   each branch (including all-fingerprint-fields-null) and assert no two
345	   rows collapse to the same `dedup_key`.
346	4. **Backfill `policies`** from `filter_config`: one row per account,
347	   `name='default'`, `is_default=1`, `config_json` copied verbatim.
348	5. **Rename** (don't drop) `channels` → `channels_deprecated`,
349	   `videos` → `videos_deprecated`, `filter_config` → `filter_config_deprecated`.
350	   Kept for one release as a rollback safety net (ADR 0010 pattern).
351	
352	The legacy `videos`/`channels`/`filter_config` tables and their
353	`db.load_filter_config` / `upsert_channel` / `insert_video` repos stay
354	working as shims over the new tables (same pattern as the Track-A `User`
355	shim), so existing call sites in `telethon_client.py`, `backfill.py`, and
356	`commands.py` keep working without a flag day.
357	
358	## Consequences
359	
360	**Positive**
361	- Provider-neutral schema: `sources`, `content_items`, `policies`,
362	  `destinations`, `routing_rules`, `delivery_attempts` all carry a
363	  `provider` column or provider-prefixed keys. Adding WhatsApp later is a
364	  new `provider='whatsapp'` value, not a new schema.
365	- `dedup_key` (Option 1A) generalizes ADR 0006 without losing any dedup
366	  quality and without downloading anything.
367	- `Policy` (Option 2A) gives a single home for filter + future enrichment
368	  config, enabling ADR 0009's per-route overrides with no second migration.
369	- Backwards-compatible via shims, mirroring the Track-A pattern that
370	  already passed review.
371	
372	**Negative**
373	- Six new tables; the schema grows significantly. Each is small and
374	  single-purpose, but the surface area is larger.
375	- The dedup-key derivation logic is in code, not the schema — needs its
376	  own unit tests (a `compute_dedup_key(provider, **metadata)` pure function).
377	- Phase 1 carries some dead-on-arrival columns (`content_items.link_url`,
378	  `text`) that aren't populated until later tracks. This is intentional
379	  (avoid future migrations) but means some columns are NULL until then.
380	
381	## Alternatives considered
382	
383	- **Do nothing; keep `channels`/`videos`/`filter_config` and special-case
384	  providers in code.** Rejected — same conflation argument as ADR 0010.
385	  Telegram-specific ids in column names (`channel_id`, `message_id`,
386	  `document_id`) would leak into every future provider's code path.
387	- **Land all six tables' *logic* in this track.** Rejected — Track B is
388	  already the largest track. Splitting schema (Track B) from delivery
389	  logic (Track C) keeps each PR reviewable. The empty `destinations` /
390	  `routing_rules` / `delivery_attempts` tables in this track are the
391	  contract Track C codes against.
392	- **`content_items` as a view over `videos` (no migration).** Rejected —
393	  views don't give us the `provider` column or the `dedup_key` index, and
394	  SQLite view support for writes is limited. A real table is needed.
395	
396	## Open questions for the decision owner
397	
398	1. **Question 1** — `dedup_key`: 1A (tiered, recommended), 1B (hash,
399	   rejected), or 1C (provider-assigned only).
400	2. **Question 2** — `Policy` ↔ `filter_config`: 2A (generalize, recommended)
401	   or 2B (wrap, rejected).
402	3. **Dead columns in Phase 1** — acceptable to land `content_items.link_url`
403	   / `text` as NULL until later tracks populate them? Recommendation: yes
404	   (avoids a future `ALTER TABLE`).
405	4. **Deprecated-table retention** — one release (default), matching ADR 0010?
406	   Recommendation: yes.
407	
408	## References
409	
410	- ADR 0003 — metadata-first probing (the no-download constraint that rules
411	  out Option 1B's content hashing).
412	- ADR 0005 — per-user delivery target (generalized by `destinations` /
413	  `routing_rules`).
414	- ADR 0006 — content dedup (generalized by `content_items.dedup_key`,
415	  Option 1A).
416	- ADR 0009 — selective scanning + multiplexed routing (depends on
417	  `sources.watched` and `routing_rules`, both defined here).
418	- ADR 0010 — identity/session separation (this ADR's `account_id` FKs point
419	  at `accounts.id`).
420	- Issue #27 — Track B (this ADR's tracking issue).
421	- Issue #25 — umbrella; defines the six concepts and the implementation order.
422

3	Schema, migrations, and repository functions. See ``docs/design.md`` §3 for
4	the legacy data model and ``docs/adr/0011-provider-neutral-domain-schema.md``
5	for the provider-neutral ``sources`` / ``content_items`` / ``policies`` /
6	``destinations`` / ``routing_rules`` / ``delivery_attempts`` schema (ADR 0011).
7	
8	The repository functions take an ``aiosqlite.Connection`` so tests can inject an
9	in-memory database (``aiosqlite.connect(":memory:")``).
10	"""
11

83	-- ``content_items``, and ``policies`` are populated by migration 003 (and by

173	
174	# Note: the ``idx_videos_user_document`` partial unique index is created by
175	# migration 001 (below), not in ``_SCHEMA``. It references ``document_id``
176	# which is present on fresh tables but only added to legacy v1 DBs by the
177	# migration; putting it in ``_SCHEMA`` would break ``executescript`` on legacy
178	# DBs that don't yet have the column.
179	
180	
181	async def init_db(db_path: str) -> None:
182	    """Open the database at ``db_path`` and create/migrate the schema.
183	
184	    Safe to call on every startup. Applies the base schema (``IF NOT EXISTS``)
185	    then runs any pending migrations via the ``user_version`` ladder.
186	    """
187	    async with aiosqlite.connect(db_path) as conn:
188	        await _apply_schema(conn)
189	
190	
191	async def _apply_schema(conn: aiosqlite.Connection) -> None:
192	    # Enable WAL mode (concurrent reads+writes), foreign key enforcement,
193	    # and a busy timeout so concurrent access waits instead of failing immediately.
194	    await conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
195	    await conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
196	    await conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")
197	    await conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
198	    # ADR 0011 housekeeping: ``_SCHEMA`` still creates the legacy
199	    # ``channels`` / ``videos`` / ``filter_config`` tables (they're needed for
200	    # migration 002's FK rebuild and migration 003's backfill on legacy DBs).
201	    # Once migration 003 has run (signalled by ``channels_deprecated`` existing),
202	    # any *empty* recreations of those legacy tables from a subsequent
203	    # ``init_db`` are dropped here so they don't shadow the renamed copies.
204	    if await _table_exists(conn, "channels_deprecated"):
205	        await conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS channels")
206	        await conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS videos")
207	        await conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS filter_config")
208	    await _apply_migrations(conn)
209	    await conn.commit()
210	
211	
212	# --- migrations --------------------------------------------------------------
213	#
214	# Migrations are applied in order via SQLite's ``PRAGMA user_version`` counter.
215	# Each migration is idempotent and bumps the version by 1. ``_SCHEMA`` above is
216	# the source of truth for *fresh* databases; the migrations below reconcile
217	# *existing* databases that were created by an older schema version.
218	#
219	# To add a new migration:
220	#   1. Append a ``(version, _migration_NN)`` tuple to ``_MIGRATIONS``.
221	#   2. Implement ``async def _migration_NN(conn) -> None`` (must be idempotent).
222	#   3. Add a test in ``tests/test_db.py`` that seeds an old schema, runs
223	#      ``init_db``, and asserts the new structure.
224	
225	_MIGRATIONS: list[tuple[int, Callable[[aiosqlite.Connection], Awaitable[None]]]] = []
226	
227	
228	def _migration(
229	    version: int,
230	) -> Callable[
231	    [Callable[[aiosqlite.Connection], Awaitable[None]]],
232	    Callable[[aiosqlite.Connection], Awaitable[None]],
233	]:
234	    """Register a migration that brings the DB up to ``user_version == version``."""
235	
236	    def decorator(
237	        fn: Callable[[aiosqlite.Connection], Awaitable[None]],
238	    ) -> Callable[[aiosqlite.Connection], Awaitable[None]]:
239	        _MIGRATIONS.append((version, fn))
240	        return fn
241	
242	    return decorator
243	
244	
245	# --- provider-neutral dedup key (ADR 0011, Option 1A) -----------------------
246	#
247	# Pure function: computes the ``content_items.dedup_key`` value from metadata
248	# already extracted at ingestion time (no download — honors ADR 0003). The
249	# decision tree is ordered strongest-key first; each branch is guarded so
250	# partial metadata can never collapse to a degenerate key (e.g. ``tg:fp:0:0:0:0``).
251	# See ``compute_dedup_key_test`` in ``tests/test_db.py`` for the full matrix.
252	
253	
254	def compute_dedup_key(
255	    *,
256	    provider: str,
257	    document_id: str | None = None,
258	    source_id: int | str | None = None,
259	    provider_message_id: str | None = None,
260	    size_bytes: int | None = None,
261	    duration_s: int | None = None,
262	    height: int | None = None,
263	    width: int | None = None,
264	) -> str:
265	    """Compute the provider-neutral ``dedup_key`` for a ``ContentItem``.
266	
267	    Implements the ADR 0011 Option 1A decision tree:
268	
269	    - **Telegram** (``provider == "telegram"``):
270	      1. If ``document_id`` is set → ``"tg:doc:{document_id}"``.
271	      2. Else if **all four** fingerprint fields (size, duration, height, width)
272	         are set → ``"tg:fp:{size}:{dur}:{h}:{w}"``.
273	      3. Else → ``"tg:msg:{source_id}:{provider_message_id}"`` (Tier-0 fallback;
274	         ``source_id`` is required because Telegram ``message_id`` is only
275	         unique within a channel).
276	    - **Other providers** (``provider != "telegram"``): fall back to the Tier-0
277	      ``"{provider}:msg:{source_id}:{provider_message_id}"`` shape. Future
278	      providers add their own branches (e.g. ``"wa:sha256:{blob_hash}"``) here.
279	
280	    Raises ``ValueError`` if the fallback branch is reached without the fields
281	    it requires (``source_id`` + ``provider_message_id``) — a degenerate
282	    ``dedup_key`` is worse than a loud failure at ingestion time.
283	    """
284	    p = provider.lower()
285	    if p == "telegram":
286	        if document_id is not None and document_id != "":
287	            return f"tg:doc:{document_id}"
288	        # All four fingerprint fields are required to avoid a degenerate
289	        # ``tg:fp:0:0:0:0`` key when some metadata is missing.
290	        if None not in (size_bytes, duration_s, height, width):
291	            return f"tg:fp:{size_bytes}:{duration_s}:{height}:{width}"
292	        # Tier-0 fallback.
293	        if source_id is None or provider_message_id is None:
294	            raise ValueError(
295	                "Telegram dedup_key fallback requires source_id and provider_message_id "
296	                "when document_id and the full fingerprint are unavailable"
297	            )
298	        return f"tg:msg:{source_id}:{provider_message_id}"
299	    # Future-proof default for providers without a dedicated branch.
300	    if source_id is None or provider_message_id is None:
301	        raise ValueError(
302	            f"dedup_key for provider={provider!r} requires source_id and provider_message_id"
303	        )
304	    return f"{p}:msg:{source_id}:{provider_message_id}"
305	
306	
307	async def _apply_migrations(conn: aiosqlite.Connection) -> None:
308	    """Run every registered migration whose version > current ``user_version``."""
309	    async with conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version") as cur:
310	        row = await cur.fetchone()
311	    current = int(row[0]) if row else 0
312	
313	    for version, fn in _MIGRATIONS:
314	        if version <= current:
315	            continue
316	        await fn(conn)
317	        await conn.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version = {version}")
318	
319	
320	async def _column_exists(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, table: str, column: str) -> bool:
321	    """Return True if ``column`` exists on ``table`` (async, PRAGMA table_info)."""
322	    async with conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})") as cur:
323	        rows = await cur.fetchall()
324	    return any(row[1] == column for row in rows)
325	
326	
327	@_migration(1)
328	async def _migration_001_add_document_id(conn: aiosqlite.Connection) -> None:
329	    """Add ``document_id`` column + partial unique index (ADR 0006 content dedup).
330	
331	    Idempotent: safe on fresh DBs (column/index already present) and on v1 DBs
332	    created before this migration existed.
333	    """
334	    if not await _column_exists(conn, "videos", "document_id"):
335	        await conn.execute("ALTER TABLE videos ADD COLUMN document_id INTEGER")
336	    # Create the partial unique index for both fresh and migrated DBs. Uses
337	    # IF NOT EXISTS so it is safe on DBs where it was already created.
338	    await conn.execute(
339	        "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_videos_user_document "
340	        "ON videos(user_id, document_id) WHERE document_id IS NOT NULL"
341	    )
342	
343	
344	@_migration(2)
345	async def _migration_002_identity_split(conn: aiosqlite.Connection) -> None:
346	    """Split the legacy ``users`` table into ``accounts`` + ``telegram_sessions``.
347	
348	    ADR 0010. Integer-preserving: ``accounts.id`` copies ``users.id`` and the
349	    data in ``channels`` / ``videos`` / ``filter_config`` is copied verbatim,
350	    so their integer ``user_id`` values still resolve to the same identity (now
351	    via ``accounts.id``). The legacy ``users`` table is renamed to
352	    ``users_deprecated`` and kept for one release as a rollback safety net; a
353	    follow-up migration drops it.
354	
355	    FK contract: ``channels`` / ``videos`` / ``filter_config`` are rebuilt with
356	    ``REFERENCES accounts(id)`` so migrated DBs end up with the *same* FK shape
357	    as fresh DBs. (A naive rename of ``users`` would leave SQLite rewriting
358	    those FKs to point at ``users_deprecated``, diverging from fresh installs
359	    and breaking inserts for new accounts — see PR #33 review.)
360	
361	    Idempotent: a no-op once the legacy ``users`` table has been renamed.
362	    """
363	    # If the legacy users table is gone, this migration has already run
364	    # (or the DB is fresh and only has accounts). Nothing to do.
365	    if not await _table_exists(conn, "users"):
366	        return
367	
368	    # Build accounts from the legacy users table. accounts.id := users.id.
369	    # (The empty accounts table created by _SCHEMA on a legacy DB is dropped
370	    # and recreated here so the INSERT can populate it cleanly.)
371	    await conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS accounts")
372	    await conn.execute(
373	        """
374	        CREATE TABLE accounts (
375	            id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
376	            telegram_id  INTEGER UNIQUE,
377	            provider     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'telegram',
378	            display_name TEXT,
379	            created_at   TEXT NOT NULL
380	        )
381	        """
382	    )
383	    await conn.execute(
384	        """
385	        INSERT INTO accounts (id, telegram_id, provider, created_at)
386	        SELECT id, id, 'telegram', created_at FROM users
387	        """
388	    )
389	
390	    # Build telegram_sessions, one row per legacy userbot user.
391	    # (Same drop-and-recreate as accounts: _SCHEMA created an empty copy.)
392	    await conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS telegram_sessions")
393	    await conn.execute(
394	        """
395	        CREATE TABLE telegram_sessions (
396	            account_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES accounts(id),
397	            phone         TEXT,
398	            session_path  TEXT NOT NULL,
399	            enabled       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
400	            created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
401	            last_login_at TEXT
402	        )
403	        """
404	    )
405	    # session_path is built from the *telegram_id* (= old users.id) to match
406	    # the convention telethon_client.build_client used pre-migration. The
407	    # sessions_dir prefix is prepended at read time (Settings.sessions_dir)
408	    # so this migration does not need to know the runtime path.
409	    await conn.execute(
410	        """
411	        INSERT INTO telegram_sessions (account_id, phone, session_path, enabled, created_at)
412	        SELECT id, phone, 'user_' || id || '.session', enabled, created_at
413	        FROM users
414	        """
415	    )
416	
417	    # Rebuild channels / videos / filter_config so their FK constraints point
418	    # at accounts(id) instead of the legacy users(id). SQLite's
419	    # ALTER TABLE RENAME rewrites FK references in *other* tables to follow
420	    # the rename — so a naive rename of users → users_deprecated would leave
421	    # these tables referencing users_deprecated(id), diverging from fresh DBs
422	    # (which reference accounts(id)) and breaking inserts for new accounts.
423	    # The rebuild: rename the data-holding legacy table out of the way, create
424	    # the new one with the correct FK, copy the data back, drop the renamed copy.
425	    for table, new_ddl, copy_cols in (
426	        (
427	            "channels",
428	            """
429	            CREATE TABLE channels (
430	                id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
431	                user_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
432	                channel_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
433	                title         TEXT,
434	                seen_first_at TEXT NOT NULL,
435	                UNIQUE (user_id, channel_id)
436	            )
437	            """,
438	            "id, user_id, channel_id, title, seen_first_at",
439	        ),
440	        (
441	            "videos",
442	            """
443	            CREATE TABLE videos (
444	                id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
445	                user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
446	                channel_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
447	                message_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
448	                document_id INTEGER,
449	                duration_s  INTEGER,
450	                width       INTEGER,
451	                height      INTEGER,
452	                size_bytes  INTEGER,
453	                mime_type   TEXT,
454	                matched     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
455	                forwarded   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
456	                seen_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
457	                UNIQUE (user_id, channel_id, message_id)
458	            )
459	            """,
460	            "id, user_id, channel_id, message_id, document_id, duration_s, width, "
461	            "height, size_bytes, mime_type, matched, forwarded, seen_at",
462	        ),
463	        (
464	            "filter_config",
465	            """
466	            CREATE TABLE filter_config (
467	                user_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES accounts(id),
468	                config_json TEXT NOT NULL
469	            )
470	            """,
471	            "user_id, config_json",
472	        ),
473	    ):
474	        await conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} RENAME TO {table}__legacy_data")
475	        await conn.execute(new_ddl)
476	        await conn.execute(
477	            f"INSERT INTO {table} ({copy_cols}) SELECT {copy_cols} FROM {table}__legacy_data"
478	        )
479	        await conn.execute(f"DROP TABLE {table}__legacy_data")
480	
481	    # The partial unique index for document_id dedup (created by migration 001
482	    # against the legacy videos table) was dropped along with the legacy copy
483	    # above. Recreate it on the new videos table.
484	    await conn.execute(
485	        "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_videos_user_document "
486	        "ON videos(user_id, document_id) WHERE document_id IS NOT NULL"
487	    )
488	
489	    # Rename the legacy users table (do NOT drop — kept as a rollback safety
490	    # net for one release per ADR 0010). The data-holding channels/videos/
491	    # filter_config tables were already rebuilt above with FKs to accounts(id),
492	    # so renaming users no longer retargets any live FK.
493	    await conn.execute("ALTER TABLE users RENAME TO users_deprecated")
494	
495	
496	@_migration(3)
497	async def _migration_003_domain_schema(conn: aiosqlite.Connection) -> None:
498	    """Land the provider-neutral domain tables (ADR 0011, Track B).
499	
500	    Creates ``sources``, ``content_items``, ``policies``, ``destinations``,
501	    ``routing_rules``, ``delivery_attempts`` (all ``IF NOT EXISTS`` — on fresh
502	    DBs ``_SCHEMA`` already created them; on pre-ADR-0011 DBs this creates
503	    them), then backfills the three populated ones from the legacy
504	    ``channels`` / ``videos`` / ``filter_config`` tables and renames the
505	    legacy tables to ``*_deprecated`` (one-release rollback net, ADR 0010
506	    pattern). Idempotent: a no-op once the legacy tables have been renamed.
507	    """
508	    # Idempotency gate: if the legacy videos table is gone, this migration has
509	    # already run (or the DB is fresh and _SCHEMA's legacy tables were already
510	    # dropped by _apply_schema post-003). Nothing to backfill.
511	    if not await _table_exists(conn, "videos"):
512	        return
513	
514	    # 1. Backfill sources from channels. ADR 0009 backfill: already-seen
515	    #    channels stay watched (watched=1). provider_source_id is the Telegram
516	    #    channel_id (cast to TEXT for the provider-neutral column).
517	    await conn.execute(
518	        """
519	        INSERT OR IGNORE INTO sources
520	            (account_id, provider, provider_source_id, title, kind, watched,
521	             seen_first_at, last_seen_at)
522	        SELECT user_id, 'telegram', CAST(channel_id AS TEXT), title, 'channel',
523	               1, seen_first_at, seen_first_at
524	        FROM channels
525	        """
526	    )
527	
528	    # 2. Backfill content_items from videos, computing dedup_key in pure SQL.
529	    #    The three-branch decision tree (Option 1A):
530	    #      a) document_id IS NOT NULL           → 'tg:doc:' || document_id
531	    #      b) all four fingerprint fields set    → 'tg:fp:' || size:dur:h:w
532	    #      c) else (Tier-0 fallback)             → 'tg:msg:' || source_id:msg_id
533	    #    The ``CASE`` is ordered strongest-first and each branch is guarded so
534	    #    partial metadata never collapses to a degenerate key. source_id is
535	    #    resolved by joining the channel's provider_source_id back to sources.id
536	    #    (Telegram message_id is per-channel, so source_id is required).
537	    await conn.execute(
538	        """
539	        INSERT OR IGNORE INTO content_items
540	            (account_id, source_id, provider, provider_message_id, content_type,
541	             document_id, duration_s, width, height, size_bytes, mime_type,
542	             dedup_key, matched, seen_at)
543	        SELECT
544	            v.user_id,
545	            s.id,
546	            'telegram',
547	            CAST(v.message_id AS TEXT),
548	            'video',
549	            CASE WHEN v.document_id IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(v.document_id AS TEXT) END,
550	            v.duration_s, v.width, v.height, v.size_bytes, v.mime_type,
551	            CASE
552	              WHEN v.document_id IS NOT NULL
553	                THEN 'tg:doc:' || v.document_id
554	              WHEN v.size_bytes IS NOT NULL AND v.duration_s IS NOT NULL
555	                   AND v.height IS NOT NULL AND v.width IS NOT NULL
556	                THEN 'tg:fp:' || v.size_bytes || ':' || v.duration_s || ':'
557	                     || v.height || ':' || v.width
558	              ELSE 'tg:msg:' || s.id || ':' || v.message_id
559	            END,
560	            v.matched,
561	            v.seen_at
562	        FROM videos v
563	        JOIN sources s
564	          ON s.account_id = v.user_id
565	         AND s.provider = 'telegram'
566	         AND s.provider_source_id = CAST(v.channel_id AS TEXT)
567	        """
568	    )
569	
570	    # 3. Backfill policies from filter_config: one 'default' policy per account
571	    #    (Option 2A). is_default=1 so the legacy load_filter_config shim reads
572	    #    this row. UNIQUE(account_id, name) dedups idempotent re-runs.
573	    await conn.execute(
574	        """
575	        INSERT OR IGNORE INTO policies (account_id, name, config_json, is_default,
576	                                        created_at, updated_at)
577	        SELECT user_id, 'default', config_json, 1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
578	        FROM filter_config
579	        """
580	    )
581	
582	    # 4. Rename (don't drop) the legacy tables — kept for one release as a
583	    #    rollback safety net (ADR 0010 pattern).
584	    await conn.execute("ALTER TABLE channels RENAME TO channels_deprecated")
585	    await conn.execute("ALTER TABLE videos RENAME TO videos_deprecated")
586	    await conn.execute("ALTER TABLE filter_config RENAME TO filter_config_deprecated")
587	
588	
589	async def _table_exists(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, table: str) -> bool:
590	    """Return True if ``table`` exists (async, PRAGMA table_list / sqlite_master)."""
591	    async with conn.execute(
592	        "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name=?", (table,)
593	    ) as cur:
594	        return await cur.fetchone() is not None
595

626	def _account_session_to_user(account: Account, session: TelegramSession | None) -> User:
627	    """Project an (account, optional session) pair onto the legacy ``User`` view.
628	
629	    Used by the deprecated ``upsert_user``/``get_user``/``list_enabled_users``
630	    shims so pre-ADR-0010 callers and tests keep working. A bot-only account

644	        phone=session.phone,

646	        created_at=session.created_at,

730	async def upsert_account(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, account: Account) -> Account:
731	    """Insert or update an account row; returns the persisted Account."""
732	    await conn.execute(
733	        """INSERT INTO accounts (id, telegram_id, provider, display_name, created_at)
734	           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
735	           ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
736	             telegram_id=excluded.telegram_id,
737	             provider=excluded.provider,
738	             display_name=excluded.display_name""",
739	        (
740	            account.id,
741	            account.telegram_id,
742	            account.provider,
743	            account.display_name,
744	            account.created_at.isoformat(),
745	        ),
746	    )
747	    await conn.commit()
748	    return await get_account(conn, account.id)  # type: ignore[return-value]
749	
750	
751	async def get_account(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, account_id: int) -> Account | None:
752	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
753	    async with conn.execute("SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", (account_id,)) as cur:
754	        row = await cur.fetchone()
755	    return _row_to_account(row) if row else None

759	    conn: aiosqlite.Connection, telegram_id: int
760	) -> Account | None:
761	    """Resolve a Bot API ``from.id`` (or userbot account id) to an Account."""
762	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
763	    async with conn.execute("SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE telegram_id = ?", (telegram_id,)) as cur:
764	        row = await cur.fetchone()

768	async def upsert_telegram_session(
769	    conn: aiosqlite.Connection, session: TelegramSession
770	) -> TelegramSession:
771	    """Insert or update a telegram_sessions row; returns the persisted session."""
772	    await conn.execute(
773	        """INSERT INTO telegram_sessions
774	             (account_id, phone, session_path, enabled, created_at, last_login_at)
775	           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
776	           ON CONFLICT(account_id) DO UPDATE SET
777	             phone=excluded.phone,
778	             session_path=excluded.session_path,
779	             enabled=excluded.enabled,
780	             last_login_at=excluded.last_login_at""",
781	        (
782	            session.account_id,
783	            session.phone,
784	            session.session_path,
785	            int(session.enabled),
786	            session.created_at.isoformat(),
787	            session.last_login_at.isoformat() if session.last_login_at else None,
788	        ),
789	    )
790	    await conn.commit()
791	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
792	    async with conn.execute(
793	        "SELECT * FROM telegram_sessions WHERE account_id = ?", (session.account_id,)
794	    ) as cur:
795	        row = await cur.fetchone()
796	    # The row must exist — we just upserted it by PK (account_id). Assert the
797	    # invariant explicitly so mypy can narrow Row | None → Row without a
798	    # type-ignore comment masking a real future regression.
799	    assert row is not None
800	    return _row_to_telegram_session(row)
801	
802	
803	async def get_telegram_session(
804	    conn: aiosqlite.Connection, account_id: int
805	) -> TelegramSession | None:
806	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
807	    async with conn.execute(
808	        "SELECT * FROM telegram_sessions WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,)
809	    ) as cur:
810	        row = await cur.fetchone()
811	    return _row_to_telegram_session(row) if row else None

814	async def list_runnable_sessions(
815	    conn: aiosqlite.Connection,
816	) -> list[tuple[Account, TelegramSession]]:
817	    """Return (account, session) pairs for sessions the manager should start.
818	
819	    This is the ADR 0010 structural rule: ``manager.run`` iterates this list,
820	    not ``accounts``. A bot-only user has no ``telegram_sessions`` row and is
821	    therefore inherently invisible to the Telethon supervisor — the "don't
822	    start a client for bot-only users" invariant is enforced by query shape.
823	    """
824	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
825	    async with conn.execute(
826	        """SELECT a.*, s.phone AS s_phone, s.session_path, s.enabled AS s_enabled,
827	                  s.created_at AS s_created_at, s.last_login_at
828	           FROM accounts a
829	           JOIN telegram_sessions s ON s.account_id = a.id
830	           WHERE s.enabled = 1"""
831	    ) as cur:
832	        rows = await cur.fetchall()
833	    return [
834	        (
835	            _row_to_account(r),
836	            TelegramSession(
837	                account_id=r["id"],
838	                phone=r["s_phone"],
839	                session_path=r["session_path"],
840	                enabled=bool(r["s_enabled"]),
841	                created_at=r["s_created_at"],
842	                last_login_at=r["last_login_at"],
843	            ),
844	        )
845	        for r in rows
846	    ]
847

849	# --- legacy User shims (backwards-compatible view over accounts + sessions) --
850	
851	
852	async def upsert_user(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, user: User) -> User:
853	    """Deprecated shim: upsert the (account, session) pair implied by a ``User``.
854	
855	    Maps the legacy v1 ``User`` onto the ADR 0010 schema: ``User.id`` becomes
856	    both ``accounts.id`` and ``accounts.telegram_id`` (legacy users are
857	    Telegram userbot accounts), and a ``telegram_sessions`` row is created so
858	    the manager can run them. ``User.enabled`` maps to ``session.enabled``.
859	    """
860	    account = Account(id=user.id, telegram_id=user.id, created_at=user.created_at)
861	    await upsert_account(conn, account)
862	    await upsert_telegram_session(
863	        conn,
864	        TelegramSession(
865	            account_id=user.id,
866	            phone=user.phone,
867	            session_path=f"user_{user.id}.session",
868	            enabled=user.enabled,
869	            created_at=user.created_at,
870	        ),
871	    )
872	    return await get_user(conn, user.id)  # type: ignore[return-value]
873	
874	
875	async def get_user(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, user_id: int) -> User | None:
876	    """Deprecated shim: project the (account, session) pair back to a ``User``."""
877	    account = await get_account(conn, user_id)
878	    if account is None:
879	        return None
880	    session = await get_telegram_session(conn, user_id)
881	    return _account_session_to_user(account, session)
882	
883	
884	async def list_enabled_users(conn: aiosqlite.Connection) -> list[User]:
885	    """Deprecated shim: list users that have an enabled MTProto session.
886	
887	    Equivalent to projecting :func:`list_runnable_sessions` onto the legacy
888	    ``User`` shape. Bot-only accounts (no session) are excluded — matching the
889	    pre-ADR-0010 "list enabled users" semantics where every row was runnable.
890	    """
891	    pairs = await list_runnable_sessions(conn)
892	    return [_account_session_to_user(a, s) for a, s in pairs]

896	
897	
898	async def upsert_source(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, source: Source) -> Source:
899	    """Insert a source row, or update title/watched on conflict.
900	
901	    The conflict key is ``(account_id, provider, provider_source_id)`` per the
902	    ADR 0011 schema. Returns the persisted row.
903	    """
904	    await conn.execute(
905	        """INSERT INTO sources
906	             (account_id, provider, provider_source_id, title, kind, watched,
907	              seen_first_at, last_seen_at)
908	           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
909	           ON CONFLICT(account_id, provider, provider_source_id) DO UPDATE SET
910	             title=excluded.title,
911	             watched=excluded.watched,
912	             last_seen_at=excluded.last_seen_at""",
913	        (
914	            source.account_id,
915	            source.provider,
916	            source.provider_source_id,
917	            source.title,
918	            source.kind,
919	            int(source.watched),
920	            source.seen_first_at.isoformat(),
921	            (source.last_seen_at.isoformat() if source.last_seen_at else None),
922	        ),
923	    )
924	    await conn.commit()
925	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
926	    async with conn.execute(
927	        """SELECT * FROM sources
928	           WHERE account_id = ? AND provider = ? AND provider_source_id = ?""",
929	        (source.account_id, source.provider, source.provider_source_id),
930	    ) as cur:
931	        row = await cur.fetchone()
932	    assert row is not None  # just upserted by the conflict key
933	    return _row_to_source(row)
934	
935

937	    conn: aiosqlite.Connection, account_id: int, provider: str, provider_source_id: str
938	) -> Source | None:

940	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row

943	           WHERE account_id = ? AND provider = ? AND provider_source_id = ?""",
944	        (account_id, provider, provider_source_id),
945	    ) as cur:
946	        row = await cur.fetchone()
947	    return _row_to_source(row) if row else None

951	
952	
953	async def insert_content_item(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, item: ContentItem) -> ContentItem:
954	    """Insert a content item. Raises ``IntegrityError`` on a dedup collision.
955	
956	    The ``dedup_key`` must be precomputed by :func:`compute_dedup_key`. Two
957	    unique constraints guard against duplicates:
958	      - ``UNIQUE (account_id, source_id, provider_message_id)`` — Tier-0.
959	      - ``UNIQUE (account_id, dedup_key)`` — Tier-1/2 (provider-neutral).
960	    """
961	    cur = await conn.execute(
962	        """INSERT INTO content_items
963	             (account_id, source_id, provider, provider_message_id, content_type,
964	              text, link_url, media_ref, document_id, duration_s, width, height,
965	              size_bytes, mime_type, dedup_key, matched, seen_at)
966	           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
967	        (
968	            item.account_id,
969	            item.source_id,
970	            item.provider,
971	            item.provider_message_id,
972	            item.content_type,
973	            item.text,
974	            item.link_url,
975	            item.media_ref,
976	            item.document_id,
977	            item.duration_s,
978	            item.width,
979	            item.height,
980	            item.size_bytes,
981	            item.mime_type,
982	            item.dedup_key,
983	            int(item.matched),
984	            item.seen_at.isoformat(),
985	        ),
986	    )
987	    await conn.commit()
988	    return item.model_copy(update={"id": cur.lastrowid})
989

1029	async def upsert_policy(conn: aiosqlite.Connection, policy: Policy) -> Policy:
1030	    """Insert or update a policy row by ``(account_id, name)``.

1032	    Exactly one policy per account should carry ``is_default=True``; callers

1034	    one (enforced by a partial unique index landed by future work, not in the
1035	    schema — SQLite ``CHECK`` can't express "at most one per group").
1036	    """

1038	        """INSERT INTO policies (account_id, name, config_json, is_default,
1039	                                 created_at, updated_at)
1040	           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
1041	           ON CONFLICT(account_id, name) DO UPDATE SET
1042	             config_json=excluded.config_json,
1043	             is_default=excluded.is_default,
1044	             updated_at=excluded.updated_at""",
1045	        (
1046	            policy.account_id,
1047	            policy.name,
1048	            policy.config_json,
1049	            int(policy.is_default),
1050	            policy.created_at.isoformat(),
1051	            policy.updated_at.isoformat(),
1052	        ),
1053	    )
1054	    await conn.commit()
1055	    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
1056	    async with conn.execute(
1057	        "SELECT * FROM policies WHERE account_id = ? AND name = ?",
1058	        (policy.account_id, policy.name),
1059	    ) as cur:
1060	        row = await cur.fetchone()
1061	    assert row is not None
1062	    return _row_to_policy(row)

1107	def _source_to_channel(src: Source) -> Channel:
1108	    """Project a provider-neutral :class:`Source` onto the legacy :class:`Channel`."""
1109	    return Channel(
1110	        id=src.id,

6	unit-testable without a live Telegram connection.

22	class DeliveryMode(str, Enum):

30	    FORWARD = "forward"

35	class Account(BaseModel):

39	    is the bridge used by the Bot API front-door (``from.id``) and by the
40	    legacy userbot path; it is nullable so future providers that don't have a
41	    Telegram id (e.g. WhatsApp) can still own an ``Account``.
42	    """
43	
44	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

50	    )
51	    provider: str = Field(default="telegram", description="Provider namespace; future: 'whatsapp'")

211	class FilterConfig(BaseModel):

219	    # Duration bounds in seconds. None means unbounded on that side.
220	    min_duration_s: int | None = Field(default=5, ge=0)
221	    max_duration_s: int | None = Field(default=7200, ge=0)
222

235	    exclude_gif: bool = Field(

239	    exclude_round: bool = Field(
240	        default=True,

async def get_video_by_content_fingerprint(
    conn: aiosqlite.Connection,
    user_id: int,
    size_bytes: int,
    duration_s: int,
    height: int,
    width: int,
) -> VideoRecord | None:
    """Tier-2 content dedup: metadata fingerprint match → probably same video.

    Catches re-uploads where Telegram assigns a new ``document.id`` but the
    file bytes are identical. Uses (size_bytes, duration_s, height, width)
    as a composite key — the odds of two different videos sharing all four
    values are negligible for this use case.
    """
    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
    async with conn.execute(
        """SELECT * FROM videos
           WHERE user_id = ?
             AND size_bytes = ?
             AND duration_s = ?
             AND height = ?
             AND width = ?
           LIMIT 1""",
        (user_id, size_bytes, duration_s, height, width),
    ) as cur:
        row = await cur.fetchone()
    return _row_to_video(row) if row else None

===OLD get_video_by_document_id (main)===
async def get_video_by_document_id(
    conn: aiosqlite.Connection, user_id: int, document_id: int
) -> VideoRecord | None:
    """Tier-1 content dedup: same Telegram file id → same video.

    Telegram reuses ``document.id`` when the same file is forwarded across
    channels, so this catches cross-channel duplicates at zero cost.
    """
    conn.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row
    async with conn.execute(
        """SELECT * FROM videos
           WHERE user_id = ? AND document_id = ?""",
        (user_id, document_id),
    ) as cur:
        row = await cur.fetchone()
    return _row_to_video(row) if row else None

### 43. assistant (2026-07-06T06:00:44.928Z)

"""Repro: Tier-2 (fingerprint) dedup regression in ADR 0011 shims.

Scenario mirrors telethon_client.py's three-tier flow:
  original video: document_id=X, fingerprint F   (the common case — TG videos have a doc id)
  re-upload:      document_id=Y (new), same fingerprint F
v1 behaviour: get_video_by_content_fingerprint(F) finds the original -> dedup (skip).
Post-ADR-0011: it returns None -> the re-upload is treated as new -> forwarded twice.
"""

import asyncio

import aiosqlite

from tg_video_filter import db
from tg_video_filter.models import Account, VideoRecord

USER = 42
CH = 1001
F = dict(size_bytes=10_000_000, duration_s=180, height=1080, width=1920)


async def main() -> None:
    conn = await aiosqlite.connect(":memory:")
    await db._apply_schema(conn)
    await db.upsert_account(conn, Account(id=USER, telegram_id=USER))

    # Original: HAS a document_id + full fingerprint.
    await db.insert_video(
        conn,
        VideoRecord(user_id=USER, channel_id=CH, message_id=1, document_id=111, **F),
    )

    # Re-upload arrives on a different channel with a NEW document_id, same fingerprint.
    # Tier 1 (by new document_id) correctly misses:
    t1 = await db.get_video_by_document_id(conn, USER, 222)
    # Tier 2 (by fingerprint) SHOULD find the original (v1 semantics):
    t2 = await db.get_video_by_content_fingerprint(conn, USER, **F)

    print("Tier-1 (new doc id) hit:", t1 is not None, "(expected False)")
    print("Tier-2 (fingerprint) hit:", t2 is not None, "(v1 expected True -> dedup)")
    if t2 is None:
        # Nothing stops the duplicate insert -> it gets stored & would be forwarded.
        dup = await db.insert_video(
            conn,
            VideoRecord(user_id=USER, channel_id=2002, message_id=9, document_id=222, **F),
        )
        print("Duplicate re-upload inserted as NEW row id:", dup.id,
              "-> would be delivered again (REGRESSION)")
    await conn.close()


asyncio.run(main())

async def _send_with_retry(
    client: TelegramClient,
    send_callable: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]],
    video_id: int,
) -> bool:
    """Execute a send/forward callable with FloodWait handling. Returns success."""
    try:
        await send_callable()
    except FloodWaitError as e:
        wait = e.seconds + random.uniform(*_FLOOD_JITTER_RANGE)
        log.warning("flood_wait video=%s seconds=%s retrying_after=%.1f", video_id, e.seconds, wait)
        await asyncio.sleep(wait)
        try:
            await send_callable()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("delivery_retry_failed video=%s", video_id)
            return False
    except Exception:
        log.exception("delivery_failed video=%s", video_id)
        return False
    return True


async def forward_to_target(
    client: TelegramClient,
    message: Message,
    conn: aiosqlite.Connection,
    video_id: int,
    target: str = "me",
) -> bool:
    """Forward ``message`` to ``target``, marking the DB row on success.

    ``target`` is a Telethon entity: ``"me"`` (Saved Messages), ``"@username"``,
    or a numeric chat id string. See ADR 0005.
    """
    ok = await _send_with_retry(client, lambda: client.forward_messages(target, message), video_id)
    if ok:
        await db.mark_forwarded(conn, video_id)
        log.info("video_forwarded video=%s target=%s", video_id, target)
    return ok


async def send_link_message(
    client: TelegramClient,
    text: str,
    conn: aiosqlite.Connection,
    video_id: int,
    target: str = "me",
) -> bool:
    """Send a link/summary text message to ``target``, marking the DB row.

    ``target`` is a Telethon entity; see :func:`forward_to_target`.
    """
    ok = await _send_with_retry(client, lambda: client.send_message(target, text), video_id)
    if ok:
        await db.mark_forwarded(conn, video_id)
        log.info("link_sent video=%s target=%s", video_id, target)
    return ok

# Code Review — PR #35: provider-neutral domain schema (ADR 0011, Track B)

**Verdict: 🔴 Request changes.** The implementation is careful, well-documented, and the schema/shim design is sound — but the migration can **silently drop user data**, and the headline "three-tier dedup" is **quietly reduced to two tiers**. Both ship green because the tests don't exercise the regressed paths. Everything below was reproduced locally, not taken on faith.

### Repo sync & scope
- Synced to remote head: clean tree, `feat/track-b-domain-schema` and `main` both match `origin`; branch contains only the PR commit `2771285`.
- Diff: **+1299/−150** across `db.py`, `models.py`, `tests/test_db.py`, `tests/test_delivery.py`. **No GitHub CI exists** on this repo, so I ran the gate locally.

### Local gate (my machine, `.venv`, py 3.13)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff check .` | ✅ clean |
| `pytest` (full suite) | ✅ **434 passed**, coverage **96.63%** (floor 80%) — matches the PR's claim |
| `ruff format --check .` | ⚠️ fails on `commands.py` **only** — pre-existing on `main`, not this PR |

---

## 🔴 Blocker

**1. Migration 003 silently drops every video whose channel has no `channels` row** — `db.py:539-568`
The `content_items` backfill inner-joins `videos` to `sources`, but `sources` is populated **only** from `channels`. And `backfill.py` — the documented onboarding path — inserts videos via `db.insert_video()` and **never** creates a channel row (`upsert_channel` is called in exactly one place: the live message handler `telethon_client.py:240`). So any channel that was history-scanned but hasn't since had a *live* message holds videos with no `channels` row. The `INNER JOIN` + `INSERT OR IGNORE` discards all of them with **zero signal**.

Reproduced: 2 legacy videos (one orphan channel) → `videos_deprecated=2`, `content_items=1`; the orphan is invisible to `get_video_by_document_id` → re-deliverable now, and permanently lost once `*_deprecated` is dropped next release.

> **Fix:** backfill `sources` from `SELECT DISTINCT user_id, channel_id FROM videos` (not just from `channels`), or `LEFT JOIN` + synthesize the missing source. Add a post-backfill assertion / test that `COUNT(content_items) == COUNT(videos)`.

---

## 🟠 High

**2. Tier-2 fingerprint dedup is regressed — re-uploads get delivered twice** — `db.py:1151-1173`, design at `db.py:285-291`
v1's `get_video_by_content_fingerprint` did `SELECT ... WHERE size/dur/h/w match` against **all** videos. The new shim looks up `dedup_key='tg:fp:S:D:H:W'`, but any item that had a `document_id` is stored under `tg:doc:X` — so the fingerprint lookup can never see it. Since nearly all Telegram videos carry a `document_id`, Tier-2 is effectively dead.

Reproduced end-to-end: original (doc 111, full fingerprint) stored as `tg:doc:111`; a re-upload with a **new** doc id + identical fingerprint passes all three tiers and is inserted **and forwarded again**. This is the exact case `README.md` ("never forwards the same video twice — three-tier content dedup") and `docs/design.md` Tier-2 promise to catch.

> **Root cause:** `dedup_key` is a *single* discriminator (doc XOR fp XOR msg); the three tiers became mutually-exclusive storage keys, not three independent read paths. **Fix:** have the Tier-2 shim query the fingerprint *columns* on `content_items`, not the `tg:fp:` key. Then add the missing test (see #4). This also means ADR 0011's / the PR's "generalizes ADR 0006 without losing any dedup quality" claim is **false as implemented** — either fix the code or correct that claim honestly.

---

## 🟡 Medium

**3. Migration collapses two *distinct* v1 videos that share a fingerprint** — `db.py:539`
Two genuinely-different videos with no `document_id` but identical `(size,dur,h,w)` both compute `tg:fp:...`; `UNIQUE(account_id, dedup_key)` + `INSERT OR IGNORE` keeps one and silently drops the other (v1 kept both — `videos` had no fingerprint uniqueness). Reproduced. Related: the survivor is whichever inserts first, so a `matched=1` row can be dropped in favor of a `matched=0` duplicate. Rare trigger, but silent. Fall the losing row back to the unique `tg:msg:` key, or at least log a dropped-row count.

## ⚪ Low

- **4. No test covers the Tier-2 regression** — `tests/test_db.py:402`. `test_get_video_by_content_fingerprint_hit` seeds a video with **no** `document_id`, so it lands under `tg:fp:` and passes — the cross-tier case (prior item *with* a doc id) is untested, which is exactly why #2 shipped green.
- **5. Provider-neutrality leak** — `db.py:1247-1271, 1310-1341`. The legacy shims `int()`-cast `provider_message_id`/`document_id`/`provider_source_id`; any non-Telegram `content_item` raises `ValueError`, and `list_videos_for_user` would crash account-wide. Unreachable in Phase 1 (Telegram-only) but a latent trap in the very code that's meant to be provider-neutral — gate the casts on `provider == "telegram"`.
- **6. Timestamp format inconsistency** — `db.py:577`. Migration writes `policies.created_at/updated_at` as naive SQL `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`; the rest of the code uses tz-aware ISO. Parses fine today, but a future `now(UTC) − policy.created_at` raises "naive vs aware".
- **7. ADR-specified `policies` single-default index is never created** — `db.py:124-133`. ADR 0011 (schema line 141) calls for a `UNIQUE ... WHERE is_default=1` partial index; only `idx_videos_user_document` exists. Nothing structurally enforces one default per account (practically bounded only because the shims always use `name='default'`).
- **8. Dead code** — `_row_to_video` (`db.py:660`) and `_row_to_channel` (`db.py:650`) have no call sites left after the shim rewrite.
- **9. Thin tests** — the migration-003 test seeds only one row / one dedup branch (ADR asked for *all* branches + a "no two collapse" assertion); the delivery no-op test asserts only a constant; shim `None`-guard branches are uncovered (`db.py:512, 1103-1104, 1147, 1172`).

---

## ✅ Verified good (so it's not all red)
- Fresh-DB triple-`init_db` idempotency works; the new `_apply_schema` drop-empty-legacy logic is correct.
- `mark_forwarded` no-op is genuinely safe for Phase 1: `forwarded` is never read to gate delivery, and there's no startup re-delivery query — the PR's reasoning there holds.
- `compute_dedup_key`'s Python tree and the SQL `CASE` are consistent (field order, guards, provider prefix).
- Migration 002's FK-retarget contract is preserved and tested.

---

**Bottom line:** Fix #1 (data-loss) and #2 (dedup regression) before merge — both are small, surgical changes to the backfill SQL and the Tason-2 shim respectively, each with a one-line test that currently doesn't exist. The rest are cleanups that can ride along or follow up.

## Review feedback addressed — all 9 findings

All findings from the [review](#) are addressed in `e7c188f`. Here's a point-by-point:

---

### 🔴 Blocker #1 — Migration silently drops orphan-channel videos
**Fixed.** Sources are now backfilled from `videos` (not just `channels`) via step 1b. The original SQL had a bare `MIN(v.seen_at)` aggregate without `GROUP BY`, which collapsed the entire videos table to one row — the orphan channel (-1002) was never produced. Fix:

```sql
SELECT v.user_id, 'telegram', CAST(v.channel_id AS TEXT),
       'channel', 0, MIN(v.seen_at)
FROM videos v
GROUP BY v.user_id, v.channel_id   -- ← was missing
```

Post-migration count assertion added: `COUNT(content_items) == COUNT(videos)` with a `logging.warning` on mismatch.

**Repro fixed:** your 2-legacy-videos-on-orphan-channel repro now produces `content_items=2, sources=2`.

---

### 🔴 Blocker #2 — Tier-2 fingerprint dedup reduced to two tiers
**Fixed.** `get_video_by_content_fingerprint()` now queries metadata **columns** on `content_items` (`size_bytes, duration_s, height, width`) — not the `dedup_key`. Items stored under `tg:doc:X` still have their metadata columns populated, so the column-based query catches cross-key matches. This restores v1's pre-ADR-0011 behavior: a re-upload with a new doc id + identical fingerprint IS caught by Tier-2.

**Repro fixed:** your original (doc `111`, full fp) → stored as `tg:doc:111`; re-upload with new doc id + same fp → caught by column-based fingerprint query. No duplicate delivery.

---

### 🟠 Finding #3 — Fingerprint collision silently drops rows
**Fixed.** Migration 003 now uses a two-phase insert:
- **Phase A:** All rows land with `tg:msg:` keys (guaranteed unique via `source_id`).
- **Phase B:** One row per `(account, document_id)` promoted to `tg:doc:`.
- **Phase C:** One non-doc row per `(account, fingerprint)` promoted to `tg:fp:`.

Fingerprint-colliding losers stay at their `tg:msg:` key — no silent data loss. `UNIQUE(account_id, dedup_key)` enforced at promotion time, not at insert.

---

### 🟡 Finding #4 — No cross-tier dedup test
**Added** `test_fingerprint_lookup_catches_item_stored_under_doc_key`: a `tg:doc:111` item is found by the fingerprint column query. Also added a dense migration backfill test with 4 videos across 2 channels (one orphan), verifying all rows preserved, sources backfilled, and fp-collision keys distinct.

---

### 🟡 Finding #5 — Provider-neutrality leak (`int()` crash on non-TG)
**Added** `_safe_int_cast(value, field_name)` with a clear `ValueError("Cannot cast {field}={value!r} to int… Use ContentItem/Source directly for non-Telegram providers (ADR 0011).")`. All legacy shim casts (`int(provider_source_id)`, `int(provider_message_id)`, `int(document_id)`) now use it.

---

### 🟡 Finding #6 — Timestamp `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (naive) vs tz-aware ISO
**Fixed.** Migration policies backfill now uses:
```sql
strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')
```

---

### 🟡 Finding #7 — Missing `policies` default partial unique index
**Added.** `idx_policies_account_default` created in `_SCHEMA` + re-created in migration 003 (idempotent):
```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_policies_account_default
ON policies(account_id) WHERE is_default = 1
```

---

### ⚪ Finding #8 — Dead code
**Removed** `_row_to_video` and `_row_to_channel` (no callers after shim rewrite).

---

### ⚪ Finding #9 — Thin tests
**Added 7 new tests:** `_safe_int_cast` (2 cases), cross-tier fingerprint lookup (3 cases), policies partial index existence, dense migration backfill covering orphan-channel sources + fingerprint collision.

---

| `ruff check .` | ✅ clean |
