24	+    """Backfill default destinations and delivery state (ADR 0011, Track C).
25	+
26	+    Creates a default destination row for each account that has a
27	+    ``filter_config_deprecated.delivery_target`` value, then creates a default
28	+    routing rule (source → default policy → destination) for each source.
29	+    Also backfills ``delivery_attempts`` rows from the legacy ``videos_deprecated``
30	+    table (one ``delivered`` attempt per previously-forwarded video to the
31	+    account's default destination).
32	+
33	+    Idempotent: skips accounts whose default destination already exists.
34	+    """
35	+    # Gate: if destinations already have data, this migration has run.
36	+    async with conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM destinations") as cur:
37	+        if (await cur.fetchone())[0] > 0:
38	+            return
39	+
40	+    if not await _table_exists(conn, "filter_config_deprecated"):
41	+        return
42	+
43	+    # 1. Backfill default destinations from filter_config_deprecated.
44	+    #    Parse the JSON delivery_target, defaulting to "me".
45	+    await conn.execute(
46	+        """
47	+        INSERT OR IGNORE INTO destinations (account_id, provider, target, kind, is_output, created_at)
48	+        SELECT user_id, 'telegram',
49	+               COALESCE(json_extract(config_json, '$.delivery_target'), 'me'),
50	+               CASE
51	+                 WHEN COALESCE(json_extract(config_json, '$.delivery_target'), 'me') = 'me'
52	+                   THEN 'saved'
53	+                 ELSE 'channel'
54	+               END,
55	+               0,
56	+               strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')
57	+        FROM filter_config_deprecated
58	+        """
59	+    )
60	+
61	+    # 2. Create a default routing rule per source (source → default policy → default destination).
62	+    await conn.execute(
63	+        """
64	+        INSERT OR IGNORE INTO routing_rules
65	+            (account_id, source_id, policy_id, destination_id, enabled, priority, created_at)
66	+        SELECT s.account_id, s.id, p.id, d.id, 1, 0,
67	+               strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')
68	+        FROM sources s
69	+        JOIN policies p ON p.account_id = s.account_id AND p.is_default = 1
70	+        JOIN destinations d ON d.account_id = s.account_id
71	+        WHERE d.target = (
72	+            SELECT COALESCE(
73	+                json_extract(fcd.config_json, '$.delivery_target'), 'me'
74	+            )
75	+            FROM filter_config_deprecated fcd
76	+            WHERE fcd.user_id = s.account_id
77	+            LIMIT 1
78	+        )
79	+        """
80	+    )
81	+
82	+    # 3. Backfill delivery_attempts from previously-forwarded videos.
83	+    await conn.execute(

86	+            (content_item_id, destination_id, route_id, status, attempt_count,
87	+             created_at, delivered_at)
88	+        SELECT ci.id, d.id, rr.id, 'delivered', 1,
89	+               vd.seen_at, vd.seen_at
90	+        FROM videos_deprecated vd
91	+        JOIN content_items ci
92	+          ON ci.account_id = vd.user_id
93	+         AND ci.provider = 'telegram'
94	+         AND ci.provider_message_id = CAST(vd.message_id AS TEXT)
95	+        JOIN sources sc

97	+         AND sc.provider_source_id = CAST(vd.channel_id AS TEXT)
98	+        JOIN destinations d ON d.account_id = vd.user_id
99	+        JOIN routing_rules rr
100	+          ON rr.account_id = vd.user_id
101	+         AND rr.source_id = sc.id
102	+         AND rr.destination_id = d.id
103	+        WHERE vd.forwarded = 1
104	+        """
105	+    )

"""Probe PR #37 (Track C) behaviors."""
import asyncio, aiosqlite, tempfile, os
from tg_video_filter import db
from tg_video_filter.models import Account, Source, ContentItem, Destination, DeliveryStatus

async def both_mode_masking():
    """BOTH mode: forward succeeds then link fails -> shared delivery_attempt row.
    Model the exact two record_delivery calls deliver() makes with one destination_id."""
    conn = await aiosqlite.connect(":memory:")
    await db._apply_schema(conn)
    await db.upsert_account(conn, Account(id=1, telegram_id=1))
    src = await db.upsert_source(conn, Source(account_id=1, provider="telegram", provider_source_id="-1"))
    dest = await db.upsert_destination(conn, Destination(account_id=1, provider="telegram", target="me"))
    item = await db.insert_content_item(conn, ContentItem(account_id=1, source_id=src.id, provider="telegram", provider_message_id="5", dedup_key="tg:msg:1:5"))
    # deliver() BOTH: forward first (success), then link (failure) — same destination_id
    await db.record_delivery(conn, content_item_id=item.id, destination_id=dest.id, success=True)
    await db.record_delivery(conn, content_item_id=item.id, destination_id=dest.id, success=False, error="link send failed")
    a = await db.get_delivery_attempt(conn, item.id, dest.id)
    await conn.close()
    print(f"[BOTH-mode] forward OK + link FAIL -> status={a.status.value!r} attempt_count={a.attempt_count} delivered_at={'set' if a.delivered_at else None}")
    print(f"           -> {'MASKS success (status=failed despite forward delivered)' if a.status==DeliveryStatus.FAILED else 'ok'}")

async def migration_me_default():
    """Migration 004 with NO delivery_target in config -> default 'me'."""
    p = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "m.db")
    legacy = """
    CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, phone TEXT, enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at TEXT NOT NULL);
    CREATE TABLE channels (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), channel_id INTEGER NOT NULL, title TEXT, seen_first_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(user_id,channel_id));
    CREATE TABLE videos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, channel_id INTEGER NOT NULL, message_id INTEGER NOT NULL, duration_s INTEGER, width INTEGER, height INTEGER, size_bytes INTEGER, mime_type TEXT, matched INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, forwarded INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, seen_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(user_id,channel_id,message_id));
    CREATE TABLE filter_config (user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, config_json TEXT NOT NULL);
    """
    async with aiosqlite.connect(p) as conn:
        await conn.executescript(legacy)
        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (111,'+1',1,'2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')")
        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO channels(user_id,channel_id,title,seen_first_at) VALUES (111,-1001,'C','2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')")
        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO videos(user_id,channel_id,message_id,matched,forwarded,seen_at) VALUES (111,-1001,42,1,1,'2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')")
        # config WITHOUT delivery_target
        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO filter_config VALUES (111, '{\"min_duration_s\":5}')")
        await conn.commit()
    await db.init_db(p)
    async with aiosqlite.connect(p) as conn:
        d = await (await conn.execute("SELECT target,kind FROM destinations WHERE account_id=111")).fetchone()
        rr = (await (await conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM routing_rules WHERE account_id=111")).fetchone())[0]
        da = await (await conn.execute("SELECT status FROM delivery_attempts")).fetchone()
    print(f"[mig 'me' default] destination={d} routing_rules={rr} delivery_attempt={da}")
    print(f"           -> {'PASS' if d==('me','saved') and rr==1 and da==('delivered',) else 'CHECK'}")

async def migration_sources_no_filterconfig():
    """Account has channels/videos but NO filter_config row -> what happens?"""
    p = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "n.db")
    legacy = """
    CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, phone TEXT, enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at TEXT NOT NULL);
    CREATE TABLE channels (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), channel_id INTEGER NOT NULL, title TEXT, seen_first_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(user_id,channel_id));
    CREATE TABLE videos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, channel_id INTEGER NOT NULL, message_id INTEGER NOT NULL, matched INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, forwarded INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, seen_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(user_id,channel_id,message_id));
    CREATE TABLE filter_config (user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, config_json TEXT NOT NULL);
    """
    async with aiosqlite.connect(p) as conn:
        await conn.executescript(legacy)
        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (222,'+2',1,'2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')")
        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO channels(user_id,channel_id,title,seen_first_at) VALUES (222,-2002,'C2','2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')")
        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO videos(user_id,channel_id,message_id,matched,forwarded,seen_at) VALUES (222,-2002,7,1,1,'2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')")
        # NO filter_config row for user 222
        await conn.commit()
    await db.init_db(p)
    async with aiosqlite.connect(p) as conn:
        dest = (await (await conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM destinations WHERE account_id=222")).fetchone())[0]
        rr = (await (await conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM routing_rules WHERE account_id=222")).fetchone())[0]
        da = (await (await conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM delivery_attempts")).fetchone())[0]
        pol = (await (await conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM policies WHERE account_id=222")).fetchone())[0]
    print(f"[mig no-filter_config] policies={pol} destinations={dest} routing_rules={rr} delivery_attempts={da} (forwarded video exists)")

async def main():
    await both_mode_masking()
    await migration_me_default()
    await migration_sources_no_filterconfig()

# Code Review — PR #37: destinations, routing_rules, delivery_attempts (ADR 0011, Track C)

**Verdict: 🟢 Solid, mergeable — no blockers.** Clean models, correct core migration, backwards-compatible delivery. ## 🟡 Medium — worth fixing before merge

**1. Malformed `config_json` aborts the upgrade → unrecoverable startup brick** (LIVE) — `db.py:694` (and the routing subquery `db.py:718`)
Migration 004 does `json_extract(config_json, '$.delivery_target')`. If any legacy `filter_config` row holds non-JSON, `json_extract` raises `OperationalError: malformed JSON`, the ladder rolls back, and **every subsequent startup re-hits it** — the app can't start. Reproduced: `config_json='not-json-at-all'` → `init_db` raises, retry still raises. Migration 003 only copied `config_json` verbatim, so 004 is the first consumer to parse it. *Reachability is low* (the app always writes valid `model_dump_json`), hence medium not blocker.
> **Fix:** `CASE WHEN json_valid(config_json) THEN json_extract(config_json,'$.delivery_target') ELSE NULL END` at both sites — a corrupt row degrades to the `'me'` default instead of bricking the upgrade.

**2. BOTH-mode delivery masking** (LATENT until Track D) — `delivery.py:214-220`, `record_delivery` `db.py:~1373`
`deliver()` BOTH mode calls `forward_to_target` then `send_link_message` with the **same** `destination_id`, so both `record_delivery` calls collide on the single `UNIQUE(content_item_id, destination_id)` row. Reproduced both directions:
- forward **ok** + link **fail** → row ends `status=failed` with `delivered_at` still set (failed link masks the successful forward);
- forward **fail** + link **ok** → the forward failure is erased.
Plus `attempt_count` over-counts (2 per single logical BOTH delivery). A Track-D retry/idempotency consumer reading `status` would re-deliver an already-forwarded video or misreport. It's dormant today (all live callers pass `destination_id=None`) but ships in this diff.
> **Fix before Track D:** record one combined outcome per destination (delivered only if the mode's required sends all succeeded; don't leave `delivered_at` on a `failed` row), or give forward/link distinct rows. The natural place to add the missing test is now.

- **Untested new paths** — the `destination_id` **failure** recording branch and the FORWARD/BOTH success paths are uncovered (`delivery.py:144,145,152,181,224`); coverage dipped 96.5→95.75%. Adding the BOTH-mode test above covers most of it.
- **Dead code** — `upsert_delivery_attempt` is exported in `__all__` but has zero callers/tests (`db.py:1320`). Test it or drop it until Track D needs it.
- **Migration edges** — an account with legacy sources but no `filter_config` gets no destination/route/history (bounded: `bootstrap.py:75` always persists one); numeric chat ids backfill as `kind='channel'` where ADR distinguishes `'chat'`; the output destination gets `is_output=0`. - **Overclaiming comment** — `models.py:216` says Track C "enforces the source/destination invariant (a channel is either source or destination, never both)" — nothing enforces it. Reword or enforce.
- **Nit** — typo "destinatinons" (`models.py:214`); comment says `filter_config.delivery_target` but the migration reads `filter_config_deprecated.config_json`.
- **Rebase** on current `main` — clears the `commands.py` format flag and de-risks the merge.

- An overstated "silent history loss" framing of the no-`filter_config` edge — the properly-scoped low version is kept above.

- `record_delivery` increment/`delivered_at` logic is correct for the single-send (FORWARD/LINK) case.

## 🟡 Medium — fix before merge

### 1. Malformed `config_json` aborts the upgrade → unrecoverable startup brick (LIVE) — `db.py:694` (+ routing subquery `db.py:718`)
Migration 004 runs `json_extract(config_json, '$.delivery_target')`. If any legacy `filter_config` row holds non-JSON, `json_extract` raises `OperationalError: malformed JSON`, the migration ladder rolls back, and **every subsequent startup re-hits it** — the app can't start.

Reachability is **low** — the live save path always writes `cfg.model_dump_json()` (valid JSON) — hence medium, not blocker.

- forward **fail** + link **ok** → the forward failure is erased;
- `attempt_count` also over-counts (2 per single logical BOTH delivery).

A future Track-D retry/idempotency consumer reading `status` would re-deliver an already-forwarded video or misreport. Dormant today (all live callers pass `destination_id=None`), but it ships in this diff.

**Fix (before Track D wires routing):** record **one combined outcome per destination** — `delivered` only when the mode's required sends all succeeded, and never leave `delivered_at` set on a `failed` row — or give the forward and link legs distinct rows / an op discriminator. Add the BOTH-mode test (below) now to pin the intended semantics.

+    tmp_path: object,

+    """Migration 004 must not crash on malformed filter_config JSON (fix #1).
+
+    A legacy filter_config row with non-JSON content must degrade to the
+    'me' default destination, not abort the migration ladder.
+    """
+    db_path = str(tmp_path) + "/bad_json.db"  # type: ignore[operator]
+    legacy_schema = """
+    CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, phone TEXT, enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at TEXT NOT NULL);
+    CREATE TABLE channels (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), channel_id INTEGER NOT NULL, title TEXT, seen_first_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE (user_id, channel_id));
+    CREATE TABLE videos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), channel_id INTEGER NOT NULL, message_id INTEGER NOT NULL, duration_s INTEGER, width INTEGER, height INTEGER, size_bytes INTEGER, mime_type TEXT, matched INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, forwarded INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, seen_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE (user_id, channel_id, message_id));
+    CREATE TABLE filter_config (user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id), config_json TEXT NOT NULL);
+    """
+    async with aiosqlite.connect(db_path) as conn:
+        await conn.executescript(legacy_schema)
+        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (111,'+1',1,'2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')")
+        await conn.execute(

+        )
+        await conn.execute(
+            "INSERT INTO videos (user_id, channel_id, message_id, duration_s, width, height, size_bytes, mime_type, matched, forwarded, seen_at) "
+            "VALUES (111, -1001, 1, 60, 1920, 1080, 1000, 'video/mp4', 1, 0, '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')"
+        )
+        # Malformed JSON — migration 004 must not crash.
+        await conn.execute("INSERT INTO filter_config VALUES (111, 'not-json-at-all')")
+        await conn.commit()
+
+    # Must not raise — the json_valid() guard degrades to 'me'.
+    await db.init_db(db_path)
+
+    async with aiosqlite.connect(db_path) as conn:
+        async with conn.execute(
+            "SELECT target, kind FROM destinations WHERE account_id=111"
+        ) as cur:

1	"""Provider-independent command parsing and execution (ADR 0011, Track D).
2	
3	Extracts command logic from the Telethon adapter (``commands.py``) so the
4	same ``/set``, ``/show`` commands work identically through a Bot API
5	front-door. The service is pure: strings in, ``CommandResult`` out — no
6	Telethon objects, no network calls.
7	
8	See ``docs/adr/0007-inline-config-commands.md`` for the command model and
9	``docs/adr/0008-bot-api-onboarding-front-door.md`` for the Bot API motivation.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import logging
15	import re
16	from dataclasses import dataclass
17	
18	import aiosqlite
19	
20	from tg_video_filter import db
21	from tg_video_filter.models import FilterConfig
22	
23	log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
24	
25	# Key into the shared engine_holder dict (imported by commands.py's adapter).
26	ENGINE_KEY = "engine"
27	
28	# --- regex patterns ----------------------------------------------------------
29	
30	_SIZE_RE = re.compile(r"^/set\s+size\s+(\d+)\s*([kmgt]?b?)$", re.IGNORECASE)
31	_LENGTH_RE = re.compile(r"^/set\s+(?:max\s+)?length\s+(\d+)\s*([smh]?)$", re.IGNORECASE)
32	_MIN_LENGTH_RE = re.compile(r"^/set\s+min\s+length\s+(\d+)\s*([smh]?)$", re.IGNORECASE)
33	_MIN_RES_RE = re.compile(r"^/set\s+min\s+(?:resolution|res)\s+(\d+)\s*p?$", re.IGNORECASE)
34	_SHOW_CONFIG_RE = re.compile(r"^/show\s+config$", re.IGNORECASE)
35	_SHOW_COMMANDS_RE = re.compile(r"^/show\s+commands$", re.IGNORECASE)
36	_EXCLUDE_RE = re.compile(r"^/set\s+exclude\s+(gif|round|nosound)\s+(on|off)$", re.IGNORECASE)
37	_EXCLUDE_HELP_RE = re.compile(r"^/set\s+exclude\s+", re.IGNORECASE)
38	_MIN_RES_HELP_RE = re.compile(r"^/set\s+min\s+(?:resolution|res)\s+", re.IGNORECASE)
39	
40	
41	# --- unit parsing ------------------------------------------------------------
42	
43	
44	def parse_size_mb(value_str: str, unit: str) -> int:
45	    """Parse a size value + unit string into mebibytes."""
46	    value = int(value_str)
47	    unit = unit.lower().rstrip("b")
48	    multipliers: dict[str, int] = {"": 1, "m": 1, "k": 1, "g": 1024, "t": 1024 * 1024}
49	    if unit in multipliers:
50	        raw = value * multipliers[unit]
51	        if unit == "k":
52	            raw = max(1, raw // 1024)
53	        return raw
54	    raise ValueError(f"Unknown size unit: {unit}")
55	
56	
57	def parse_duration_s(value_str: str, unit: str) -> int:
58	    """Parse a duration value + unit string into seconds."""
59	    value = int(value_str)
60	    unit = unit.lower()
61	    multipliers: dict[str, int] = {"": 1, "s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600}
62	    if unit in multipliers:
63	        return value * multipliers[unit]
64	    raise ValueError(f"Unknown time unit: {unit}")
65	
66	
67	# --- formatting helpers ------------------------------------------------------
68	
69	
70	def _format_duration(seconds: int | None) -> str:
71	    if seconds is None:
72	        return "unlimited"
73	    if seconds == 0:
74	        return "0s"
75	    if seconds < 60:
76	        return f"{seconds}s"
77	    if seconds < 3600:
78	        m, s = divmod(seconds, 60)
79	        return f"{m}m{s}s" if s else f"{m}m"
80	    h, rem = divmod(seconds, 3600)
81	    m, s = divmod(rem, 60)
82	    parts = f"{h}h"
83	    if m:
84	        parts += f"{m}m"
85	    if s:
86	        parts += f"{s}s"
87	    return parts
88	
89	
90	def _format_size(mb: int | None) -> str:
91	    if mb is None:
92	        return "unlimited"
93	    if mb == 0:
94	        return "0MB"
95	    if mb >= 1024:
96	        gb = mb / 1024
97	        if gb == int(gb):
98	            return f"{int(gb)}GB"
99	        return f"{gb:.1f}GB"
100	    return f"{mb}MB"
101	
102	
103	def format_config(cfg: FilterConfig) -> str:
104	    """Format a ``FilterConfig`` as a readable message (Telegram markdown)."""
105	    lines = [
106	        "📋 **Current Filter Configuration**",
107	        "",
108	        f"⏱️  **Duration:** {_format_duration(cfg.min_duration_s)} - {_format_duration(cfg.max_duration_s)}",
109	        f"📐 **Min resolution:** {'≥ ' + str(cfg.target_height) + 'p' if cfg.target_height else 'disabled'}",
110	        f"💾 **Max file size:** {_format_size(cfg.max_size_mb)}",
111	        f"📬 **Delivery mode:** `{cfg.delivery_mode.value}`",
112	        f"📍 **Delivery target:** `{cfg.delivery_target}`",
113	        "",
114	        "🚫 **Content exclusions:**",
115	        f"   GIF/animated: {'❌ excluded' if cfg.exclude_gif else '✅ allowed'}",
116	        f"   Round videos: {'❌ excluded' if cfg.exclude_round else '✅ allowed'}",
117	        f"   Silent (no audio): {'❌ excluded' if cfg.exclude_nosound else '✅ allowed'}",
118	    ]
119	    return "\n".join(lines)
120	
121	
122	def format_commands() -> str:
123	    """Return a help message listing all available commands."""
124	    return "\n".join(
125	        [
126	            "🤖 **Available Commands**",
127	            "",
128	            "📋 **Filter config**",
129	            "`/show config` — Show current filter settings",
130	            "`/set size <N><unit>` — Set max file size (e.g. `/set size 10MB`)",
131	            "   Units: `MB` (default), `GB`, `KB` — case-insensitive, optional trailing `B`",
132	            "`/set length <N><unit>` — Set max video duration (e.g. `/set length 15m`)",
133	            "   or `/set max length <N><unit>` — same as above",
134	            "   Units: `s` (default), `m`, `h` — case-insensitive",
135	            "`/set min length <N><unit>` — Set min video duration (e.g. `/set min length 5s`)",
136	            "   Units: `s` (default), `m`, `h` — case-insensitive",
137	            "`/set min resolution <N>p` — Set min video height (e.g. `/set min resolution 720p`)",
138	            "   or `/set min res <N>p` — same as above",
139	            "",
140	            "🚫 **Content exclusions** (all off by default)",
141	            "`/set exclude gif on|off` — Exclude Telegram GIFs/animated documents",
142	            "`/set exclude round on|off` — Exclude circular video messages",
143	            "`/set exclude nosound on|off` — Exclude videos without audio\n"
144	            "   Note: GIFs are usually silent; `exclude nosound` will catch most GIFs too.",
145	            "",
146	            "🔍 **Backfill**",
147	            "`/backfill [N][hdw]` — Scan last N hours/days/weeks of channel history (default 90d)",
148	            "`/stop` — Cancel running backfill",
149	            "",
150	            "\u2139\ufe0f  **Help**",
151	            "`/show commands` — Show this help message",
152	        ]
153	    )
154	
155	
156	# --- command result ----------------------------------------------------------
157	
158	
159	@dataclass
160	class CommandResult:
161	    """The output of executing a command — provider-independent.
162	
163	    The adapter (Telethon or Bot API) uses ``reply_text`` to send the response
164	    and ``config_changed`` to decide whether to hot-reload the filter engine.
165	    """
166	
167	    reply_text: str = ""
168	    config_changed: bool = False
169	
170	
171	# --- command service ---------------------------------------------------------
172	
173	
174	class CommandService:
175	    """Provider-independent command execution.
176	
177	    Parses a command string against an account's current config and DB,
178	    returning a ``CommandResult``. No Telethon objects involved — pure string
179	    in, effects out. The Telethon adapter (``commands.py``) handles the
180	    transport (checking message.out, sending the reply); the Bot API adapter
181	    (future) calls ``handle()`` with the ``from.id`` from the update.
182	
183	    Usage::
184	
185	        svc = CommandService()
186	        result = await svc.handle(user_id, text, conn, current_cfg)
187	        if result.config_changed:
188	            engine_holder["engine"] = FilterEngine(current_cfg)
189	        await send_reply(result.reply_text)
190	    """
191	
192	    # -- public API -----------------------------------------------------------
193	
194	    async def handle(
195	        self,
196	        user_id: int,
197	        text: str,
198	        conn: aiosqlite.Connection,
199	        current_cfg: FilterConfig,
200	    ) -> CommandResult:
201	        """Parse and execute a command text, returning the reply + change flag."""
202	        text = text.rstrip()
203	
204	        # --- /set size <value><unit> ----------------------------------------
205	        m = _SIZE_RE.match(text)
206	        if m:
207	            value_str, unit = m.group(1), m.group(2) or ""
208	            try:
209	                new_mb = parse_size_mb(value_str, unit)
210	            except ValueError:
211	                return CommandResult("❌ Invalid size format. Use e.g. `/set size 10MB`.")
212	            if new_mb < 1:
213	                return CommandResult("❌ Size must be at least 1 MB (`FilterConfig` constraint).")
214	            cfg = await self._update(conn, user_id, current_cfg, max_size_mb=new_mb)
215	            return CommandResult(
216	                f"✅ Max file size set to **{_format_size(new_mb)}**.\n\n{format_config(cfg)}",
217	                config_changed=True,
218	            )
219	
220	        # --- /set length <value><unit> --------------------------------------
221	        m = _LENGTH_RE.match(text)
222	        if m:
223	            value_str, unit = m.group(1), m.group(2) or ""
224	            try:
225	                new_secs = parse_duration_s(value_str, unit)
226	            except ValueError:
227	                return CommandResult("❌ Invalid duration format. Use e.g. `/set length 15m`.")
228	            min_secs = current_cfg.min_duration_s or 0
229	            if new_secs < min_secs:
230	                return CommandResult(
231	                    f"❌ Max duration ({_format_duration(new_secs)}) must be "
232	                    f">= min duration ({_format_duration(min_secs)})."
233	                )
234	            cfg = await self._update(conn, user_id, current_cfg, max_duration_s=new_secs)
235	            return CommandResult(
236	                f"✅ Max duration set to **{_format_duration(new_secs)}**.\n\n{format_config(cfg)}",
237	                config_changed=True,
238	            )
239	
240	        # --- /set min length <value><unit> ----------------------------------
241	        m = _MIN_LENGTH_RE.match(text)
242	        if m:
243	            value_str, unit = m.group(1), m.group(2) or ""
244	            try:
245	                new_min = parse_duration_s(value_str, unit)
246	            except ValueError:
247	                return CommandResult("❌ Invalid duration format. Use e.g. `/set min length 5s`.")
248	            max_secs = current_cfg.max_duration_s or 0
249	            if max_secs > 0 and new_min > max_secs:
250	                return CommandResult(
251	                    f"❌ Min duration ({_format_duration(new_min)}) must be "
252	                    f"<= max duration ({_format_duration(max_secs)})."
253	                )
254	            cfg = await self._update(conn, user_id, current_cfg, min_duration_s=new_min)
255	            return CommandResult(
256	                f"✅ Min duration set to **{_format_duration(new_min)}**.\n\n{format_config(cfg)}",
257	                config_changed=True,
258	            )
259	
260	        # --- /set min resolution <N>p --------------------------------------
261	        m = _MIN_RES_RE.match(text)
262	        if m:
263	            new_height = int(m.group(1))
264	            if new_height < 1:
265	                return CommandResult("❌ Resolution must be at least 1p.")
266	            cfg = await self._update(conn, user_id, current_cfg, target_height=new_height)
267	            return CommandResult(
268	                f"✅ Min resolution set to **{new_height}p**.\n\n{format_config(cfg)}",
269	                config_changed=True,
270	            )
271	
272	        if _MIN_RES_HELP_RE.match(text):
273	            return CommandResult(
274	                "❌ Usage: `/set min resolution <N>p`  (e.g. `/set min resolution 720p`)"
275	            )
276	
277	        # --- /set exclude <gif|round|nosound> <on|off> ----------------------
278	        m = _EXCLUDE_RE.match(text)
279	        if m:
280	            what = m.group(1).lower()
281	            state = m.group(2).lower()
282	            enabled = state == "on"
283	            labels = {"gif": "GIF/animated", "round": "round videos", "nosound": "silent videos"}
284	            field_map = {
285	                "gif": "exclude_gif",
286	                "round": "exclude_round",
287	                "nosound": "exclude_nosound",
288	            }
289	            cfg = await self._update(conn, user_id, current_cfg, **{field_map[what]: enabled})
290	            return CommandResult(
291	                f"✅ {labels[what]} exclusion: **{'ON' if enabled else 'OFF'}**."
292	                f"\n\n{format_config(cfg)}",
293	                config_changed=True,
294	            )
295	
296	        if _EXCLUDE_HELP_RE.match(text):
297	            return CommandResult(
298	                "❌ Usage: `/set exclude <gif|round|nosound> <on|off>`\n"
299	                "Example: `/set exclude gif on`"
300	            )
301	
302	        # --- /show config ---------------------------------------------------
303	        if _SHOW_CONFIG_RE.match(text):
304	            cfg = await db.load_filter_config(conn, user_id)
305	            return CommandResult(format_config(cfg))
306	
307	        # --- /show commands -------------------------------------------------
308	        if _SHOW_COMMANDS_RE.match(text):
309	            return CommandResult(format_commands())
310	
311	        # Not a recognised command — return empty result (noise).
312	        return CommandResult()
313	
314	    # -- internal -------------------------------------------------------------
315	
316	    async def _update(
317	        self,
318	        conn: aiosqlite.Connection,
319	        user_id: int,
320	        current: FilterConfig,
321	        max_size_mb: int | None = None,
322	        max_duration_s: int | None = None,
323	        min_duration_s: int | None = None,
324	        target_height: int | None = None,
325	        exclude_gif: bool | None = None,
326	        exclude_round: bool | None = None,
327	        exclude_nosound: bool | None = None,
328	    ) -> FilterConfig:
329	        """Apply partial updates to the account's config, persist, and return."""
330	        updates: dict[str, object] = {}
331	        if max_size_mb is not None:
332	            updates["max_size_mb"] = max_size_mb
333	        if max_duration_s is not None:
334	            updates["max_duration_s"] = max_duration_s
335	        if min_duration_s is not None:
336	            updates["min_duration_s"] = min_duration_s
337	        if target_height is not None:
338	            updates["target_height"] = target_height
339	        if exclude_gif is not None:
340	            updates["exclude_gif"] = exclude_gif
341	        if exclude_round is not None:
342	            updates["exclude_round"] = exclude_round
343	        if exclude_nosound is not None:
344	            updates["exclude_nosound"] = exclude_nosound
345	        cfg = current.model_copy(update=updates) if updates else current
346	        await db.save_filter_config(conn, user_id, cfg)
347	        log.info(
348	            "config_updated user=%s max_size_mb=%s min_duration_s=%s max_duration_s=%s "
349	            "target_height=%s exclude_gif=%s exclude_round=%s exclude_nosound=%s",
350	            user_id,
351	            cfg.max_size_mb,
352	            cfg.min_duration_s,
353	            cfg.max_duration_s,
354	            cfg.target_height,
355	            cfg.exclude_gif,
356	            cfg.exclude_round,
357	            cfg.exclude_nosound,
358	        )
359	        return cfg
360	
361	
362	__all__ = [
363	    "ENGINE_KEY",
364	    "CommandResult",
365	    "CommandService",
366	    "_format_duration",
367	    "_format_size",
368	    "format_config",
369	    "format_commands",
370	    "parse_duration_s",
371	    "parse_size_mb",
372	]

    """Load the current config, apply partial updates, persist, and return."""
    cfg = await db.load_filter_config(conn, user_id)
    if max_size_mb is not None:
        cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"max_size_mb": max_size_mb})
    if max_duration_s is not None:
        cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"max_duration_s": max_duration_s})
    if min_duration_s is not None:
        cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"min_duration_s": min_duration_s})
    if target_height is not None:
        cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"target_height": target_height})
    if exclude_gif is not None:
        cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"exclude_gif": exclude_gif})
    if exclude_round is not None:
        cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"exclude_round": exclude_round})
    if exclude_nosound is not None:
        cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"exclude_nosound": exclude_nosound})
    await db.save_filter_config(conn, user_id, cfg)
    log.info(
        "config_updated user=%s max_size_mb=%s min_duration_s=%s max_duration_s=%s "
        "target_height=%s "
        "exclude_gif=%s exclude_round=%s exclude_nosound=%s",
        user_id,
        cfg.max_size_mb,
        cfg.min_duration_s,
        cfg.max_duration_s,
        cfg.target_height,
        cfg.exclude_gif,
        cfg.exclude_round,
        cfg.exclude_nosound,
    )
    return cfg

    async def on_command(event: object) -> None:
        message = getattr(event, "message", None)
        if message is None:
            return

        # Only respond to messages the user sent to themselves.
        if not getattr(message, "out", False):
            return
        peer = getattr(message, "peer_id", None)
        peer_user_id = getattr(peer, "user_id", None) if peer else None
        if peer_user_id != user.id:
            return

        text: str = getattr(message, "message", "") or ""
        # Strip trailing whitespace so mobile keyboards don't silently
        # reject commands (e.g. "/show config " → "/show config").
        text = text.rstrip()
        client: TelegramClient = getattr(event, "client", None)  # type: ignore[assignment]

        # --- /set size <value><unit> ----------------------------------------
        m = _SIZE_RE.match(text)
        if m:
            value_str, unit = m.group(1), m.group(2) or ""
            try:
                new_mb = parse_size_mb(value_str, unit)
            except ValueError:
                await _reply(client, message, "❌ Invalid size format. Use e.g. `/set size 10MB`.")
                return
            if new_mb < 1:
                await _reply(
                    client, message, "❌ Size must be at least 1 MB (`FilterConfig` constraint)."
                )
                return
            cfg = await _update_config(conn, user.id, max_size_mb=new_mb)
            engine_holder[ENGINE_KEY] = FilterEngine(cfg)

# Code Review — PR #38: extract `CommandService` (ADR 0011, Track D)

**Verdict: 🟢 Clean, behavior-preserving refactor — mergeable, no blockers.** The extraction is faithful: I found **zero behavioral divergences** from the old inline logic, and the independent multi-agent equivalence pass (46-input battery) agreed. Coverage went **up**. The three findings below are all test-quality/hygiene.

**Ramp-up:** synced; branch `feat/track-d-command-service` (one commit `22abe72`) → `main`, current with main, `MERGEABLE/CLEAN`.

**Gate (local):** ✅ `ruff check` + `format` clean · ✅ **482 passed @ 97.05%** (up from 96.52%, floor 80%).

**Behavioral equivalence — verified two ways:**
- Regex patterns **byte-identical**; branch order unchanged; `rstrip` preserved (moved into `handle()`).
- All reply strings **identical** — the "difference" my first grep flagged was the old code's implicit f-string concatenation (`f"✅…." f"\n\n{format_config}"`); the new single literal produces the same output.
- 23-command battery through the new `CommandService` → correct replies + `config_changed` for every case; the workflow's 46-input battery found no divergence.
- Adapter loads `current_cfg` fresh and reloads to rebuild the engine — equivalent to the old in-`_update_config` reload (save→load round-trips).
- All 17 `test_commands.py` imports satisfied by the re-export shim (and that unchanged suite passes).

## Findings (all non-blocking)

**🟡 Medium (low end) — service tests don't verify persistence** — `tests/test_command_service.py`
The 20 new tests assert only `config_changed` + a reply substring; none reload the config to confirm the *right field* got the *right value*. Verified by mutation: swapping `field_map["gif"] → "exclude_round"` (or writing `max_size_mb` into `min_duration_s`) still passes all 20 service tests — the reply label is derived from `labels[what]`, decoupled from `field_map`. A real regression is caught only *incidentally* by the unchanged `test_commands.py` (`assert loaded.max_size_mb == 512`). The dedicated service file — the natural home for that assertion — doesn't check its core responsibility.
> **Fix:** in the success-path tests add `loaded = await db.load_filter_config(conn, USER_ID); assert loaded.max_size_mb == 100` (etc.).

**⚪ Low — redundant config reads per self-message** — `commands.py:70`
The adapter calls `db.load_filter_config` for *every* self-message that clears the out/peer gate — including plain non-command text (old code never touched the DB there) — and `/show config` reads twice (adapter + inside `handle()`). No behavioral/correctness impact; just extra SQLite reads on the message hot path. Optional micro-opt (skip the load for non-commands, or pass `current_cfg` into the `/show config` branch).

**⚪ Low — dead `except ValueError` + misnamed test** — `command_service.py` / `tests/test_command_service.py:93`
The `except ValueError` branches for size/length/min-length are **unreachable** — the regex `(\d+)` + constrained unit group guarantee the parsers never raise (verified by enumerating all capturable units). `test_set_size_invalid_format_returns_empty` actually exercises the *noise* path (its input doesn't match `_SIZE_RE`), so the name misleads. Both are pre-existing patterns carried over. Either delete the dead branches (+rename the test) or leave as-is.

## ✅ Verified good
- Faithful extraction: identical patterns/strings/order/transport, complete re-exports, clean Telethon-free service ready for the Bot API adapter.
- `model_copy(update=…)` skips Pydantic validation in both old and new — **preserved**, and all constraint-violating inputs are guarded by explicit pre-checks (size<1, height<1, duration bounds), so no invalid config can persist.
- Coverage rose; `commands.py` command paths now fully mapped through the service.

---

**Bottom line:** ship it. Worth adding the persistence assertions (medium) since the new test file should own that check, but nothing here blocks. Want me to **post this to PR #38** (comment, as before)?

### 253. assistant (2026-07-06T09:06:35.506Z)

**HIGH finding confirmed and ADR-backed.** The gate only skips when a source row *exists* and is unwatched; a **new** channel (no row) falls through → gets scanned/delivered → then `upsert_channel` creates it `watched=True`. So new channels are **auto-watched (opt-out)** — directly inverting ADR 0009's locked *"opt-in: DEFAULT 0… new channels default to watched=0 and must be explicitly watched."* The PR's "matching the ADR 0009 backfill" justification conflates the migration (existing→1) with new-channel behavior (should be →0).

### 262. assistant (2026-07-06T09:17:36.808Z)

## Code review — selective source scanning (ADR 0009, Track E)

**Verdict: 🔴 Request changes.** The commands and DB layer are clean and well-tested, but the **ingestion gate inverts ADR 0009's central, explicitly-locked opt-in contract** — new channels are auto-watched, so the feature doesn't actually gate anything for a fresh user. Every finding was reproduced locally against `db87cc0` (posting as a comment — GitHub blocks the author from a formal request-changes).

### Gate
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest` | ✅ 492 passed, coverage **97.10%** (floor 80%) |
| `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` | ✅ clean |

Green — but the suite passing is misleading here: the core gate logic is uncovered (see #4), and the `@username` test passes against unrealistic data (#2).

---

## 🔴 Blocker — new channels are auto-watched, inverting ADR 0009 opt-in — `telethon_client.py:189-190` + `db.upsert_channel` (`db.py:~1402`)

The gate returns early only when a source row **already exists** and is unwatched:
```python
src = await db.get_source_by_provider_id(conn, user.id, "telegram", str(channel_id))
if src is not None and not src.watched:
    return
```
A **brand-new** channel has no row → `src is None` → the gate falls through → the message is deduped, filtered, **and delivered** → then `upsert_channel` lazily creates the source with `watched=True` (hardcoded). So every new channel is auto-scanned and permanently watched from its first message.

This directly contradicts **ADR 0009 (Accepted)**:
- line 37-38: *"The default is locked as **opt-in: `DEFAULT 0`**, so a freshly-onboarded user scans nothing until they explicitly /watch."*
- line 130-131: *"New channels discovered after the migration default to `watched = 0` and must be explicitly watched."*
- line 44: *"return early if watched is false, **before any dedup or filter work**."* (here the first message is fully processed and delivered before the row even exists.)

**Failure scenario:** a freshly-onboarded user who has watched nothing receives a video from any channel they're a member of → it's evaluated and **delivered** to their target, and the channel is now permanently watched. The PR's stated goal ("make the system manageable instead of blindly processing every visible channel") isn't achieved for new channels — it's opt-out.

The PR frames `watched=True` as "matching the ADR 0009 backfill," but the ADR's `watched=1` back-compat applies **only to channels seen pre-migration** (`UPDATE … WHERE seen_first_at IS NOT NULL`, line 126) — not to channels first seen *after* the migration.

**Fix:** treat an absent row as unwatched and skip before dedup/filter, lazily creating the row `watched=0` for `/channels` discoverability:
```python
if src is None or not src.watched:
    # lazily upsert the source with watched=0 (discoverability), then:
    return
```
And the ingest-path lazy creation (`upsert_channel`, and the `insert_video` upsert at `db.py:~1578`) must not force `watched=True` for newly-seen channels — only the migration backfill may set `watched=1`.

---

## 🟡 Medium

**2. `/watch`/`/unwatch` by `@username` or channel name are non-functional for real sources** — `command_service.py:_resolve_source`
`_resolve_source` only looks up by `provider_source_id`, which for real Telegram sources is always the **numeric** channel id (`str(channel_id)`). So `/watch @somechannel` (and by name) returns *"not found"* even for a known channel — only the numeric id works. Reproduced against a realistic source (numeric id, name in `title`): `@name` and `<name>` both fail, `-100…` works. The passing `test_watch_by_username` seeds an **unrealistic** source (`provider_source_id="@mychan"`), giving false confidence. ADR line 64 specifies `/watch <#name|id>` (name **or** id). *(Impact is bounded because `/channels` prints the numeric id users copy — but half the advertised interface is dead and mis-tested.)*
> **Fix:** resolve by `title`/username (case-insensitive) in addition to numeric id; fix the test to seed a realistic source.

**3. Ingestion gate has zero test coverage** — `telethon_client.py:184` (inside a `# pragma: no cover` handler)
The core gating behavior (skip unwatched, handle new) is untested — a test would have caught #1. Extract a pure helper, e.g. `async def should_ingest(conn, account_id, channel_id) -> bool`, and unit-test the watched / unwatched / **absent** cases.

---

## ⚪ Low

- **4. `format_commands()` omits the new commands** — `/watch`, `/unwatch`, `/channels`, `/watchlist` are undiscoverable via `/show commands` (`command_service.py:129`). Add a "Source scanning" section + extend `test_format_commands_includes_all_sections`.
- **5. `lstrip("@")` strips *multiple* leading `@`** (`command_service.py:~417`) — `@@foo` normalizes to `foo`. Use `target[1:] if target.startswith("@") else target`.

## Disclosed scope cut (noting because it compounds #1)
`/channels` lists only already-seen sources; it does **not** enumerate `client.get_dialogs()` to surface untrafficked channels (ADR lines 48-54). The PR body discloses this as deferred — fine as scope — but combined with #1 the intended opt-in discoverability flow (lazy row `watched=0` → appears in `/channels` → user opts in) doesn't exist yet in either half.

## ✅ Verified good
- `set_source_watched` / `list_account_sources` are clean and **tested with persistence assertions** (nice — addresses the Track D feedback); command handlers well-structured; `/channels` / `/watchlist` / error paths covered.
- Gate is correctly placed *before* dedup (efficient) — the placement is right, only the `src is None` default is wrong.

---

**Bottom line:** the blocker is a small, surgical fix (gate on `src is None or not src.watched`, lazy-create `watched=0`) but it's essential — without it, Track E doesn't actually make scanning selective for new channels. #2/#3 are worth doing in the same pass since they're the exact places a test would have caught #1.

---

# Re-review round — Track E fix (`ceabe7f`, merged as #39 → `main` `3bfb1da`)

The author pushed a fix **and merged it**. Good news: the fix addresses all six of my original findings. Bad news: **it introduced a new blocker that's now in `main`** — I reproduced it.

## ✅ Original findings — addressed
| # | Finding | Fix | Verified |
|---|---------|-----|----------|
| 🔴 1 | New channels auto-watched | Default → `watched=False`; gate skips absent sources; extracted `should_ingest_source()` that lazily creates a `watched=0` row | intent correct ✓ (but see below) |
| 🟡 2 | `/watch @name` broken | Added title substring lookup (`/watch My` matches title "My Channel") | works ✓ |
| 🟡 3 | Gate untested | Extracted `should_ingest_source` + 3 unit tests | ✓ |
| ⚪ 4 | `format_commands` omits commands | Added "Source scanning" section + test asserts it | ✓ |
| ⚪ 5 | `lstrip("@")` strips multiple | `removeprefix("@")` | ✓ |

## 🔴 New blocker introduced by the fix (now in `main`) — a watched channel un-watches itself after one video

The fix flipped `upsert_channel` and `insert_video` to upsert sources with `watched=False`. But `upsert_source`'s `ON CONFLICT` does `watched=excluded.watched`, and the live handler **still calls both after the gate** (`telethon_client.py:248` `upsert_channel`, `:271` `insert_video`). So ingesting a video from a watched channel **overwrites the user's `watched` flag back to `False`**.

Reproduced end-to-end:
```
after /watch            : watched = True
should_ingest (msg 1)   : True          ← msg 1 ingests
after upsert_channel     : watched = False   ← clobbered
after insert_video       : watched = False
should_ingest (msg 2)   : False         ← channel silently un-watched
```
**Effect:** `/watch <channel>` works for exactly **one** video, then the channel stops being watched. The feature is still broken — differently, and now silently/intermittently. The suite is green because no test exercises "watch → ingest → still watched?" (the exact integration the `# pragma: no cover` handler hides).

**Root cause:** `watched` is user-controlled state; ingestion-path upserts must not clobber it. **Fix:** drop `watched=excluded.watched` from `upsert_source`'s `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` so an existing row keeps its `watched` value (only `set_source_watched`, a direct `UPDATE`, changes it). New rows still get their INSERT value; the migration backfill still sets `watched=1` via direct insert. I checked — no caller relies on `upsert_source` toggling `watched`, so this is safe.

## Minor (carried, low)
- `/watch @username` still can't match a real source (no username column); the title path covers name-based lookup, so acceptable. Title match is a first-substring match, so `/watch a` could hit an unintended channel — worth an exact-match-first tiebreak later.

---

**Bottom line:** the fix resolved the original blocker's *intent* but traded it for an equally-breaking, untested regression that's now merged. This needs a follow-up (one-line `ON CONFLICT` change + a `watch → ingest → still watched` regression test).

Since #39 is already merged, want me to:
1. **Open a GitHub issue** documenting the regression + fix + repro,
2. **Post a comment** on the merged PR #39, and/or
3. **Draft the follow-up fix** (branch off `origin/main`: drop `watched=excluded.watched`, add the regression test) — like the #36 cleanup?

I'll hold for your call on which.

## [PR #41 — fix(scanning): don't clobber user-controlled `watched` on source upsert](https://github.com/avidullu/telegram-video-filter/pull/41)

**State:** OPEN · MERGEABLE · CLEAN (+61/−9) off `origin/main`.

**The regression it fixes** (the one #39's fix introduced, now in `main`): the ingestion path re-touches the source on every message via `upsert_channel` + `insert_video`, and `upsert_source`'s `ON CONFLICT` overwrote `watched` with the shims' hardcoded `False` — so a `/watch`-ed channel got silently un-watched after its first ingested video.

**The fix:**
```sql
ON CONFLICT(...) DO UPDATE SET
  title=COALESCE(excluded.title, sources.title),   -- was: title=excluded.title  (insert_video passed NULL → erased the name)
  last_seen_at=excluded.last_seen_at               -- removed: watched=excluded.watched
```
`watched` is user-controlled state (only `set_source_watched` / `/watch`,`/unwatch` change it), so it's set only on a new row's INSERT and never clobbered on conflict. I confirmed no caller relies on the old behavior (the commands use a direct `UPDATE`; the migration uses a direct `INSERT`).

**Verification (all reproduced locally):**
- New `test_watched_source_survives_ingestion_upserts` (watch → ingest → still watched + title intact) and the updated conflict test **both fail against pre-fix `db.py` and pass after** — proven by reverting `db.py` in isolation.
- Full suite **496 passed @ 96.94%** (+1 test), `ruff check` + `format` clean.

**Process:** drafted in an isolated worktree off `origin/main` (shared checkout untouched), staged explicit paths, confirmed only my commit `5791e29` was ahead before pushing; worktree removed, `main` left clean.

Note it's a **separate PR** (#41) rather than a comment on the merged #39, since the regression lives in `main` now. When it's reviewed/merged, that closes out the Track E selective-scanning contract properly (opt-in default *and* `/watch` that sticks). Want me to also drop a short note on #39 linking to #41 for traceability?

# ADR 0012: Policy pipeline — explainable, tiered, user-customizable content gates

- **Status**: Proposed
- **Date**: 2026-07-06
- **Decision owner**: project owner
- **Tracking issue**: #31 (Track F of the provider-neutral umbrella, #25)
- **Depends on**: ADR 0011 (Track B — domain schema, `policies` table)

## Context

The system today evaluates every matched video against a single `FilterConfig`
(per account, via `policies.config_json`). The filter is **flat**: all rules
run unconditionally, the output is a boolean (`matched`), and there is no
way to express topic preferences, security policy, or why a specific video
passed or failed.

Track F defines a **policy pipeline** — an ordered sequence of stages that
run before delivery — so the system can express richer decisions, explain
them, and defer expensive work until after cheap rejections.

### What we have today (post-Track-E)

| Concept | Current state |
|---|---|
| `FilterConfig` / `Policy` | One JSON blob per account. Flat duration/resolution/size/exclude rules. AND semantics. |
| `FilterEngine` | Evaluates all rules; returns `FilterResult(passed, reasons)`. |
| `policies` table | One row per account (is_default=1). `config_json` is the `FilterConfig` blob. |
| Security / topic / deep-inspect | Nothing. Codec/keyword/MIME filters and ffprobe were deferred to v2 in the original plan. |

### What we want

A **policy** should be a pipeline of ordered **stages**, each with a
well-defined cost, inputs, and explainable output. The pipeline runs
**after** dedup and **before** delivery. Users should be able to express
topic preferences ("I like AI and philosophy videos"), security rules
("reject links from sketchy domains"), and view **why** a specific item was
accepted or rejected.

## Decision

### Stage model — four ordered tiers

The pipeline is split into four tiers, ordered by cost (cheapest first).
Later stages only run if all earlier stages pass:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Policy Pipeline                         │
│                                                            │
│  Tier 1 — Metadata gates  (always runs, zero I/O)         │
│     duration, resolution, size, codec, mime, GIF/round    │
│     → extends today's FilterEngine                        │
│                                                            │
│  Tier 2 — Topic preferences  (opt-in, metadata-only)       │
│     source allowlist, keyword match, channel topic tags    │
│     → user-expressed interests filter the stream           │
│                                                            │
│  Tier 3 — Content safety  (opt-in, metadata + light I/O)   │
│     URL/domain reputation, file metadata sanity,           │
│     caption text scanning                                  │
│     → cheap checks; no download                            │
│                                                            │
│  Tier 4 — Deep inspection  (opt-in, heavy I/O)             │
│     ffprobe, perceptual hash, downloaded content scan      │
│     → gated behind explicit user opt-in + budget           │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Stage interface — `PolicyStage`

Each stage is a pure function (or async function for I/O stages) that
takes a `PolicyContext` and returns a `StageResult`:

```python
@dataclass
class PolicyContext:
    """Immutable snapshot of what the stage can inspect."""
    content_item: ContentItem        # from ADR 0011
    source: Source                   # the source it came from
    policy: Policy                   # the owning policy config

@dataclass
class StageResult:
    passed: bool
    reason: str                      # human-readable explanation
    stage_name: str                  # e.g. "duration-gate", "url-reputation"
    metadata: dict[str, object] = field(default_factory=dict)  # for explainability UI

class PolicyStage(Protocol):
    """A single gate in the pipeline. Stateless; may be async for I/O stages."""
    async def evaluate(self, ctx: PolicyContext) -> StageResult: ...
```

The pipeline evaluates stages in order and **short-circuits** on the first
failure (don't waste I/O on an already-rejected item). The accumulated
`StageResult` list is the **explanation trace** — every decision is
auditable.

### Topic preferences — Tier 2

Topic preferences are stored as a JSON array in `policies.config_json`
under a `topics` key:

```json
{
  "min_duration_s": 5,
  "topics": {
    "include": ["AI", "Philosophy", "Soccer"],
    "exclude": ["Politics", "Crypto"],
    "mode": "any"  // "any" = match any include topic; "all" = match all
  }
}
```

Topic matching is **metadata-only** in v1: source title substring match,
message caption keyword match, and (future) channel topic tags from
Telegram's channel metadata. No ML classification in the design — that's
a separate issue.

### Security stages — Tier 3

Security stages are **opt-in** and configured per-policy. The design
defines three initial stages (implementation deferred to separate issues):

1. **Source allowlist**: reject items from sources not in the `allowlist`
   (an explicit list of trusted provider_source_ids).
2. **URL/domain reputation**: check links in captions against a
   configurable blocklist. Metadata-only — no page fetch.
3. **Duplicate suppression**: enhanced dedup that compares by
   `content_fingerprint` across accounts (already handled by
   `content_items.dedup_key`; this stage adds cross-policy duplicate
   detection within an account's delivery streams).

Each security stage records its decision in `StageResult.metadata` for
explainability (e.g. `{"blocked_domain": "sketchy-site.com"}`).

### Deep inspection — Tier 4

Deep inspection (ffprobe, perceptual hash, downloaded content scan) is
**gated behind explicit opt-in** because it violates ADR 0003's
no-download principle. The opt-in is per-policy (`deep_inspect: true` in
`config_json`) and the stage has a **budget** (max bytes per item, max
concurrent downloads) enforced by the policy engine.

This tier is explicitly deferred to a follow-up issue — the design only
**reserves the slot** in the pipeline model so it doesn't require a schema
migration when implemented.

### Policy evaluation flow (post-dedup, pre-delivery)

```python
async def evaluate_pipeline(
    ctx: PolicyContext,
    stages: list[PolicyStage],
) -> tuple[bool, list[StageResult]]:
    results: list[StageResult] = []
    for stage in stages:
        result = await stage.evaluate(ctx)
        results.append(result)
        if not result.passed:
            return False, results  # short-circuit
    return True, results
```

The caller (telethon_client or future Bot API handler) records the
results via `delivery_attempts.last_error` (for failed items) or a new
`policy_decisions` table (for explainability — deferred to implementation).

### Schema — minimal changes

**No schema migration** is required for this design. The `policies` table
already holds a `config_json` JSON blob. The pipeline is a code concept:

- `policies.config_json` gains optional `topics`, `allowlist`,
  `security_checks`, `deep_inspect` keys — all backwards-compatible with
  the existing `FilterConfig` Pydantic model (extra fields are ignored).
- Future `policy_decisions` table (deferred) would store the explanation
  trace for debugging: `(content_item_id, policy_id, stage_name, passed,
  reason, metadata_json, evaluated_at)`.

### Implementation phasing (future issues)

| Phase | Scope | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| **F1** — Policy engine prototype | `PolicyStage` protocol, `evaluate_pipeline()`, wire into live-message handler | None |
| **F2** — Topic preferences | `topics` config parsing, source title/caption keyword matching | F1 |
| **F3** — Source allowlist | `allowlist` config, skip non-allowlisted sources | F1 |
| **F4** — URL/domain reputation | Domain blocklist, caption link extraction | F1 |
| **F5** — Deep inspection | ffprobe/perceptual hash, download budget enforcement | F1, ADR 0003 waiver |
| **F6** — Policy decisions table | Audit trail storage, explainability UI | F1 |
| **F7** — Explainability endpoint | `/why <content_item_id>` command showing the explanation trace | F6 |

Each phase is a separate, mergeable PR — none are bundled here. This ADR
only defines the **design contract** the phases code against.

## Consequences

**Positive**
- Unifies topic, security, and quality gates into a single explainable
  framework — no ad-hoc if-chains scattered across handlers.
- Cheap gates always run first; expensive enrichment is only reached for
  items that pass the cheap gates.
- `StageResult` list provides an audit trail (explainability) without
  additional DB lookups at decision time.
- Backwards-compatible: `policies.config_json` already exists; adding
  optional keys requires no migration.
- Each implementation phase is independently shippable behind feature
  flags.

**Negative**
- Four tiers add conceptual complexity vs. today's flat filter.
- `PolicyStage` protocol requires all stages to conform to the same
  interface, which may be awkward for deeply different checks
  (metadata-only vs. I/O-heavy). Mitigated by the `metadata` dict
  catch-all.
- Topic matching is string-based substring matching in Phase 1 — not
  semantic. A future ML stage would replace it, but it's good enough for
  a v1.
- Deep inspection violates ADR 0003 and must be explicitly opt-in with a
  budget to avoid runaway costs.

## Alternatives considered

- **Do nothing; keep flat FilterConfig.** Rejected — the umbrella exists
  to dissolve the conflation of quality, topic, and security into a
  single boolean. A pipeline is the natural generalization.
- **Inline each stage in the handler** (no protocol). Rejected — makes
  it impossible to test stages independently, reorder them, or add new
  ones without touching the hot path.
- **Use a rules engine / DSL.** Rejected — over-engineered for <100
  users. A Python list of callables is simpler, testable, and
  introspectable.
- **Bundle all phases into a single PR.** Rejected — scope discipline.
  Each phase is independently shippable; this ADR defines the shared
  interface they code against.

## Open questions for the decision owner

1. **`StageResult.metadata` shape** — dict or typed per-stage? Recommend:
   dict for Phase 1 (flexible), typed in Phase 2 (once the shape
   stabilizes).
2. **Policy decisions table** — store every decision, or only failures?
   Recommend: every decision (explainability), with a TTL-based cleanup
   for old traces.
3. **Topic matching** — substring only, or regex/glob? Recommend:
   substring (case-insensitive) for v1; natural-language matching in a
   follow-up.
4. **Deep inspection budget** — per-item byte limit or per-account
   bandwidth cap? Recommend: per-item limit (10 MB default) with a
   per-account monthly cap enforced at the app level.

## References

- ADR 0003 — metadata-first probing (the no-download principle that Tier
  4 must opt in to violate).
- ADR 0009 — selective channel scanning (the `topics.allowlist` concept
  generalizes `sources.watched`).
- ADR 0011 — provider-neutral domain schema (the `policies` table this
  design extends, `ContentItem` as the `PolicyContext` input).
- Issue #31 — Track F (this ADR's tracking issue).
- Issue #25 — umbrella; this is the final track.

The workflow confirmed all 19 findings (0 refuted; they dedupe to ~9 distinct issues), corroborating my two headline concerns and adding several. Three independent agents empirically verified the config round-trip erasure, so that one's rock-solid. Here's the consolidated design review.

---

# Design review — PR #40 (draft, docs-only): ADR 0012 Policy Pipeline

**This is a design doc (Proposed), so no gate applies — feedback below is on the design contract.** The core model is sound: a **cost-ordered, short-circuiting four-tier pipeline** with a `PolicyStage` protocol and a `StageResult` explanation trace is a clean, testable generalization of today's flat filter, and the F1–F7 phasing + "alternatives considered" show good discipline. But several load-bearing claims and interfaces have gaps that would break the F-phases if coded as written. Everything below was verified against the code / other ADRs.

## 🔴 High — resolve before the F-phases

**1. The backwards-compat claim is inverted — "extra fields are ignored" means *dropped*, so the config never persists.**
The ADR's central compat mechanism ("adding optional `topics`/`allowlist`/`security_checks`/`deep_inspect` keys — backwards-compatible, extra fields ignored") is the *opposite* of what's needed. `FilterConfig` uses Pydantic's default `extra='ignore'`, which **discards** unknown keys. So the moment a user runs any `/set`, `load_filter_config` parses `config_json` → `FilterConfig` (dropping the pipeline keys) and `save_filter_config` re-serializes via `model_dump_json()` — **silently erasing the entire Track-F config**. Verified empirically (FilterConfig drops the keys on round-trip). It's rescuable (`upsert_policy` writes `config_json` verbatim, so a raw-dict path survives), but the ADR directs implementers down the shim path that loses data and specifies no alternative.
> **Fix:** state the persistence mechanism explicitly — either extend `FilterConfig` with typed optional fields (a real `models.py` change, contradicting "code concept only"), set `extra='allow'` and stop round-tripping through it, or parse `config_json` as a raw dict. As written it *guarantees* config loss.

**2. Storing rejection reasons in `delivery_attempts.last_error` is a category error.**
Rejected items short-circuit *before* delivery, so there's no `(content_item_id, destination_id)` pair and no `delivery_attempts` row to write to — `record_delivery` (Track C) requires a `destination_id` and only runs on the delivery path. It also conflates "delivery transport failed" with "policy rejected." The only viable store is the deferred `policy_decisions` table (F6) — which means **F6 is a hard dependency of any persisted explainability, and F7's `/why` has nothing to read until F6 lands.**
> **Fix:** drop the `last_error` path; say rejected-item traces are in-memory/log-only until F6, and fix the phasing dependencies.

**3. Tier 2/3 depend on caption text that the pipeline is never given.**
Tier 2 ("message caption keyword match"), Tier 3 ("caption text scanning"), and F4 (link extraction) all need `content_item.text` — but it's **never populated on the live path** (verified: only read, never written; ADR 0011 left it NULL for Phase 1). Capturing captions at ingestion is unstated new work these phases silently depend on.

## 🟡 Medium

**4. `PolicyContext` can't support the I/O tiers it defines.** It holds only `(content_item, source, policy)` — no client/message handle — so Tier 3 (light I/O) and Tier 4 (download/ffprobe) can't fetch anything. Add a `fetcher`/`download(budget)` capability, or split the protocol for I/O stages.

**5. Tier 3 "Source allowlist" duplicates `sources.watched` (Track E, just merged).** An unwatched source is never ingested, so a Tier-3 allowlist never sees it — dead stage. And the References call it `topics.allowlist` (Tier 2) while the body puts "Source allowlist" in Tier 3 — pick one home, or drop it (watched *is* the source gate).

**6. Tier 3 "Duplicate suppression" overlaps the pre-pipeline dedup** (`content_items.dedup_key`, Track B, runs before the pipeline). The "cross-policy/cross-destination" scope has no supporting schema — drop it or specify it concretely.

**7. F1's "Dependencies: None" understates the work.** The live handler still runs on the legacy `VideoRecord` shim, not the `ContentItem`/`Source`/`Policy` that `PolicyContext` requires — F1 first has to thread those through the hot path.

**8. AND-only short-circuit vs. include/exclude/OR topic semantics.** The pipeline is pure AND across tiers, but topics need include-OR / exclude-veto logic. It's handled *within* the Tier-2 stage — the ADR should say so explicitly rather than leave the tension.

**9. Tier 4 references ADR 0003 but never amends it.** The phasing cites a nonexistent "ADR 0003 waiver." Add a formal "ADR 0003 is amended for opt-in deep inspection under budget" section rather than an informal reference.

## ⚪ Low
- **10.** The `topics` example contradicts the prose (says "JSON array," shows an object) and contains a `//` comment — **invalid JSON** for a real `config_json`.

## ✅ Worth keeping (design strengths)
Cost-ordered short-circuit is the right instinct; `PolicyStage`/`StageResult` is clean and independently testable; "no migration, `config_json` already exists" is *structurally* true (only the round-trip is broken); phasing and the rejected-alternatives (rules-engine/DSL for <100 users) are well-judged.

---

**Bottom line for a draft:** the skeleton is good; the two things that most need fixing before F1 are the **config persistence mechanism** (#1) and the **explainability storage** (#2), plus wiring the **caption/context inputs** (#3/#4) into the contract so F2–F5 have what they read.

## Design review — ADR 0012 Policy Pipeline (draft, docs-only)

Reviewing this as a **design contract** (no code, so no test gate). The core model is sound — a **cost-ordered, short-circuiting four-tier pipeline** with a `PolicyStage` protocol and a `StageResult` explanation trace is a clean, testable generalization of today's flat filter, and the F1–F7 phasing + "alternatives considered" show good discipline. But several load-bearing claims and interfaces have gaps that would break the F-phases if coded as written. Everything below was verified against the code / the other ADRs.

## 🔴 High — resolve before the F-phases

**1. The backwards-compat claim is inverted — "extra fields are ignored" means *dropped*, so pipeline config never persists.**
`FilterConfig` uses Pydantic's default `extra='ignore'`, which **discards** unknown keys. So the moment a user runs any `/set`, `load_filter_config` parses `config_json` → `FilterConfig` (dropping `topics`/`allowlist`/`security_checks`/`deep_inspect`) and `save_filter_config` re-serializes via `model_dump_json()` — **silently erasing the entire Track-F config**. Verified empirically (the keys don't survive the round-trip). It's rescuable — `upsert_policy` writes `config_json` verbatim, so a raw-dict path survives — but the ADR directs implementers down the shim path that loses data and specifies no alternative.
> **Fix:** state the persistence mechanism explicitly — extend `FilterConfig` with typed optional fields (a real `models.py` change, contradicting "code concept only"), set `extra='allow'` and stop round-tripping through it, or parse `config_json` as a raw dict. As written it guarantees config loss.

**2. Storing rejection reasons in `delivery_attempts.last_error` is a category error.**
Rejected items short-circuit *before* delivery, so there's no `(content_item_id, destination_id)` pair and no `delivery_attempts` row to write to — `record_delivery` (Track C) requires a `destination_id` and only runs on the delivery path. It also conflates "delivery transport failed" with "policy rejected." The only viable store is the deferred `policy_decisions` table (F6) — so **F6 is a hard dependency of any persisted explainability, and F7's `/why` has nothing to read until F6 lands.**
> **Fix:** drop the `last_error` path; state that rejected-item traces are in-memory/log-only until F6, and fix the phasing dependencies.

**3. Tier 2/3 depend on caption text the pipeline is never given.**
Tier 2 ("message caption keyword match"), Tier 3 ("caption text scanning"), and F4 (link extraction) all need `content_item.text` — but it's **never populated on the live path** (verified: only read, never written; ADR 0011 left it NULL for Phase 1). Capturing captions at ingestion is unstated new work these phases silently depend on.

## 🟡 Medium

**4. `PolicyContext` can't support the I/O tiers it defines.** It holds only `(content_item, source, policy)` — no client/message handle — so Tier 3 (light I/O) and Tier 4 (download/ffprobe) can't fetch anything. Add a `fetcher`/`download(budget)` capability, or split the protocol for I/O stages.

**5. Tier 3 "Source allowlist" duplicates `sources.watched` (Track E, just merged).** An unwatched source is never ingested, so a Tier-3 allowlist never sees it — dead stage. And the References call it `topics.allowlist` (Tier 2) while the body puts "Source allowlist" in Tier 3 — pick one home, or drop it (watched *is* the source gate).

**6. Tier 3 "Duplicate suppression" overlaps the pre-pipeline dedup** (`content_items.dedup_key`, Track B, runs before the pipeline). The "cross-policy/cross-destination" scope has no supporting schema — drop it or specify it concretely.

**7. F1's "Dependencies: None" understates the work.** The live handler still runs on the legacy `VideoRecord` shim, not the `ContentItem`/`Source`/`Policy` that `PolicyContext` requires — F1 first has to thread those through the hot path.

**8. AND-only short-circuit vs. include/exclude/OR topic semantics.** The pipeline is pure AND across tiers, but topics need include-OR / exclude-veto logic. It's handled *within* the Tier-2 stage — the ADR should say so explicitly rather than leave the tension.

**9. Tier 4 references ADR 0003 but never amends it.** The phasing cites a nonexistent "ADR 0003 waiver." Add a formal "ADR 0003 is amended for opt-in deep inspection under budget" section rather than an informal reference.

## ⚪ Low
**10.** The `topics` example contradicts the prose (says "JSON array," shows an object) and contains a `//` comment — **invalid JSON** for a real `config_json`.

## ✅ Worth keeping
Cost-ordered short-circuit is the right instinct; `PolicyStage`/`StageResult` is clean and independently testable; "no migration, `config_json` already exists" is *structurally* true (only the round-trip is broken); the phasing and rejected alternatives (rules-engine/DSL for <100 users) are well-judged.

---

**Bottom line for a draft:** the skeleton is good. The two things that most need fixing before F1 are the **config persistence mechanism** (#1) and the **explainability storage** (#2), plus wiring the **caption/context inputs** (#3/#4) into the contract so F2–F5 have what they read.

<sub>🤖 Design review with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). Claims verified against the code and ADRs 0003/0009/0011. Multi-agent adversarial pass: 19 findings → ~9 distinct, 0 refuted.</sub>

126	+"""Policy pipeline primitives for ADR 0012.
127	+
128	+The policy layer is deliberately small and framework-free in F1: stages receive
129	+an immutable context, return a structured result, and the evaluator stops on
130	+the first failure. Later Track F phases add concrete stages.
131	+"""
132	+
133	+from __future__ import annotations
134	+
135	+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
136	+from typing import Protocol
137	+
138	+from tg_video_filter.models import ContentItem, Policy, Source
139	+
140	+
141	+@dataclass(frozen=True)
142	+class PolicyContext:
143	+    """Immutable snapshot available to a policy stage."""
144	+
145	+    content_item: ContentItem
146	+    source: Source
147	+    policy: Policy
148	+    fetcher: object | None = None
149	+    budget: object | None = None
150	+
151	+
152	+@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	+class StageResult:
154	+    """Outcome of one policy stage."""
155	+
156	+    passed: bool
157	+    reason: str
158	+    stage_name: str
159	+    metadata: dict[str, object] = field(default_factory=dict)
160	+
161	+    @staticmethod
162	+    def pass_(stage_name: str, reason: str, **metadata: object) -> StageResult:
163	+        return StageResult(
164	+            passed=True,
165	+            reason=reason,
166	+            stage_name=stage_name,
167	+            metadata=metadata,
168	+        )
169	+
170	+    @staticmethod
171	+    def fail(stage_name: str, reason: str, **metadata: object) -> StageResult:
172	+        return StageResult(
173	+            passed=False,
174	+            reason=reason,
175	+            stage_name=stage_name,
176	+            metadata=metadata,
177	+        )
178	+
179	+
180	+class PolicyStage(Protocol):
181	+    """A single stateless gate in the policy pipeline."""
182	+
183	+    async def evaluate(self, ctx: PolicyContext) -> StageResult:
184	+        """Evaluate ``ctx`` and return a stage result."""
185	+        ...
186	+
187	+
188	+async def evaluate_pipeline(
189	+    ctx: PolicyContext,
190	+    stages: list[PolicyStage],
191	+) -> tuple[bool, list[StageResult]]:
192	+    """Evaluate stages in order and short-circuit on the first failure."""
193	+    results: list[StageResult] = []
194	+    for stage in stages:
195	+        result = await stage.evaluate(ctx)
196	+        results.append(result)
197	+        if not result.passed:
198	+            return False, results
199	+    return True, results
200	+
201	+
202	+__all__ = [
203	+    "PolicyContext",
204	+    "PolicyStage",
205	+    "StageResult",
206	+    "evaluate_pipeline",
207	+]

149	+@dataclass(frozen=True)
150	+class TopicPreferences:
151	+    """Parsed ADR 0012 topic preference config."""
152	+
153	+    include: tuple[str, ...] = ()
154	+    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()
155	+    mode: str = "any"
156	+

160	+
